:::note[Written against main]
This page follows `main` at 8742d79, and it differs from the copy in HotLoop core 4.18.11, the latest release. Parts of it may be newer than what you have installed. The [release notes](/releases/) say what moved.
:::

Every call the Gateway answers over HTTP, what it needs, what it takes and what
it gives back. The web UI uses nothing else: there is no private API behind the
screens, so anything the UI can do, a script can do with the same calls and the
same permissions.

This file is checked against the code. `TestAPIReferenceMatchesRoutes` in
`internal/api` reads every route the server registers and fails the build if one
is missing from the [endpoint index](#endpoint-index), if the index lists one
that does not exist, or if the permission written here is not the one the code
checks. `TestAPIReferencePermissionsTable` does the same for the
[permissions table](#permissions) against `internal/auth`. So the list of routes
and who may call them is not a description of the API as it once was. The
request and response shapes below were taken from a running Gateway; the tests
do not check those, so if you change a handler, change its section here too.

Deeper background lives with each feature: [AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/),
[ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/), [EQUIPMENT.md](/iot/equipment/),
[AUTOMATIONS.md](/iot/automations/), [REPORTS.md](/gateway/reports/),
[FLEET.md](/gateway/fleet/), [NOTIFY.md](/iot/notifications/), [BACKUP.md](/iot/backup/) and
[MCP.md](/iot/mcp/). This file is the list; those are the reasons.

## Conventions

### Where it lives

Everything is on the app's one HTTP port (`HOTLOOP_LISTEN_ADDR`, `:8080` by
default). Behind a proxy that serves the app under a path, set
`HOTLOOP_BASE_PATH` and the Gateway strips it, so `/hotloop/api/devices` and
`/api/devices` are the same call. The paths below are written without it.

### Logging in: a cookie or a bearer token

Every `/api/` route needs a session, except logging in (with a password, or with
a PIN or badge at a kiosk panel), inbound webhooks and alarm acknowledge links, each of which carries its own proof in the request.
`POST /api/auth/login` answers with a token and also sets it as the
`iiot_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure when the request came in
over TLS or with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`). A browser uses the cookie and
never sees the token. A script sends the token instead:

```
Authorization: Bearer 3f9c...e1
```

Both are the same session, checked the same way. A session lasts
`HOTLOOP_AUTH_SESSION_TTL` (12 hours by default). Without one, every `/api/`
route answers:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="hotloop"

{"error":"not logged in"}
```

or `"the session is invalid or has expired"` for a token that was revoked or ran
out, or `"this account no longer has access"` for an account that was disabled.

With `HOTLOOP_AUTH_INSECURE=true` there is no login at all: nothing is checked,
every permission below is granted to everyone, and the name recorded against a
write comes from the proxy's `X-EmberNET-User`, `X-Forwarded-User`,
`X-Auth-Request-User`, `X-Remote-User` or `X-Forwarded-Email` header, or
`operator` if none is set. That is only reasonable behind a NetworkPolicy that
lets nothing but the dashboard proxy reach the pod. See
[AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/#running-without-a-login).

MCP is separate: it has its own bearer token (`HOTLOOP_MCP_TOKEN`) and never
looks at a session. See [MCP](#mcp).

### Permissions

A logged-in user holds a list of permissions, from their role or set on the
account explicitly. A route that needs one the user does not hold answers:

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"error":"viewer1 does not have the \"values.write\" permission"}
```

The [permissions table](#permissions) says which role holds what.

### Errors

Every failure the API itself produces is JSON of one shape:

```json
{"error": "value is outside the tag's configured range: 120 is outside 0..95"}
```

`/readyz` adds a `detail`, and a failed service call adds the writes it made.
The message is written for the person reading it: it says what was wrong and,
where there is one, what to do instead. Show it as it is.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | The request is wrong: a malformed body, a field that fails validation, an unknown field, a missing parameter, an unknown service |
| 401 | No session, an expired one, or a wrong password on login |
| 403 | The user lacks the permission, or the write gate refused the write on policy: writes switched off, the tag not armed, the entity disabled |
| 404 | The thing named in the path or body does not exist |
| 409 | It already exists, or it is in the wrong state for this: an alarm that is not shelved, a node that still has children, an entity with no known state to toggle, a script that is already running, a recipe that was refused or is already being applied |
| 422 | A value the write gate refused on its merits: out of the tag's range, off an entity's step |
| 502 | The device answered, with an error of its own, and the body is its words; or a recipe started and not every target landed, and the body says which went out and which did not |
| 503 | The device is not connected, or the alarm engine is not running |
| 500 | A fault inside the server. The body is `internal error (ref …); the server log has the detail under that ref` and nothing more, and the log has the whole error under that ref. The one 500 with a real message is a button press whose release did not go out, because that message says exactly what to check |

Anything the API can't place is a 500, never a 400. A database outage answered
as 400 tells the operator they typed something wrong, and they go hunting for a
typo that isn't there.

Two failures do not come from the API and are plain text, not JSON: a path that
matches no route answers `404 page not found`, and a known path called with the
wrong method answers `405 method not allowed`.

A refused write is never a 500. A plant screen that shows a policy refusal as a
server fault teaches operators to ignore errors.

### Bodies

Request bodies are JSON, at most 4 MiB (an inbound webhook, 1 MiB). **Unknown
fields are refused**, not ignored:

```json
{"error":"request body: json: unknown field \"x\""}
```

A misspelled setting that is silently dropped looks exactly like one that
worked, so the decoder says no instead.

`POST` and `PUT` on devices, tags, alarms, automations, fleet members and
reports replace the whole object: a field left out takes its zero value, and a
boolean left out is `false`. Read, change, send back. The exceptions are the
entity and equipment `PUT`s, which change only the fields you send, and device
credentials, which are kept when left out (see below).

### Secrets are write-only

A credential stored in a device (a broker password, an HTTP header, a password
in the address) is never sent back, to any role, admin included. It shows as
`[redacted]`:

```json
"config": {"clientId": "docs-api-tankfarm", "password": "[redacted]", "username": "tank"}
```

When you save the device, send the placeholder (or leave the key out) to keep
the stored value, send a new value to replace it, and send `""` or `null` to
clear it. A new device cannot be saved with the placeholder, and a save that
moves the device to a different host with a kept credential is refused, so a
stored password cannot be walked off to a listener of somebody else's. The full
rules are in [AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/#device-credentials-are-write-only). The same goes
for every other credential the Gateway holds: settings show `set` or
`not set`, diagnostics scrub credentials out of outbound MCP targets, and nothing in this API
returns a password hash or a session token except the one login hands you.

### camelCase, except where it is snake_case

Most of the API is camelCase (`deviceId`, `pollIntervalMs`, `createdAt`), as it
has been since the first version and as the EmberNet dashboard's `TagValue`
contract requires.

The entity, state, service, equipment and label endpoints are snake_case
(`entity_id`, `last_changed`, `parent_id`, `label_id`). That is on purpose: the entity API uses the common entity, state and service shape, so that anything which already speaks it speaks this, and the equipment tree is the entity model's area registry, shaped
for the same consumers. Where the two meet, each side keeps its own case: a
device has `equipmentId`, an entity has `equipment_id`.

### Times, durations, and tag keys

- **Timestamps** are RFC 3339 in UTC, with fractional seconds when there are
  any: `2026-09-27T20:21:58.255869Z`. The display timezone setting changes what
  the UI shows, never what the API returns.
- **A time that hasn't happened is left out.** A rule that has never run has
  no `lastRun`, a device never polled has no `lastPoll` or `lastGood`, an alarm
  nobody acknowledged has no `ackedAt`, a fleet member never seen has no
  `lastSeen`. A missing time field means never. You will never see Go's zero
  time, `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, in a response or a stream event. A dozen
  fields used to send it, and the automations screen showed a rule that had
  never run as last run 739887 days ago. A test reads every route and every
  time field in the code to keep it that way.
- **Sparklines** are the exception: `timestamps` there is Unix milliseconds,
  because it goes straight into a chart.
- **Durations** say their unit in the name: `pollIntervalMs`, `onDelaySec`,
  `minutes`, `durationMs`. `uptime` in status is a Go duration string (`11m13s`).
- **A tag key** is `device/tag`, the form every `?tag=` parameter and `tag`
  field takes. Tag names may contain slashes (OPC UA paths, MQTT topics), so
  only the first slash separates: `plc-1/Line/Zone 1` is tag `Line/Zone 1` on
  device `plc-1`.
- **A numeric query parameter** that is not a number is ignored and the default
  is used, so `?limit=abc` is `?limit` unset.
- **Empty lists** are `[]`, never `null`, in every response and every stream
  event, at any depth. You don't need a null check before `.length`. A `null`
  you do see is never a list: it's one of the documented nullable fields, like
  an entity's `equipment_id` or a root node's `parent_id`. A list field marked
  optional can still be left out entirely.

### Optional features

Fleet, notifications, backups and scheduled reports are off unless their
`HOTLOOP_*_ENABLED` variable is set. With the feature off, its list route
still answers 200, with `"configured": false` and an empty list, so a screen
can say "not enabled" instead of "nothing here". Every other route of that
feature answers 400 with an error naming the variable:

```json
{"error":"backups are not enabled (HOTLOOP_BACKUP_ENABLED)"}
```

`GET /api/sites` does the same when no outbound MCP servers are configured.

### Not in this product

HotLoop ships as IoT, Edge, Gateway, and Edge Relay out of one codebase, and a feature a
product doesn't have isn't switched off, it isn't in the binary. On IoT, Edge, and Gateway its routes still answer, after the same permission check, with a 404 that says so and
names both ends, so a script can tell "wrong box" from "wrong URL":

```json
{"error":"scheduled reports are part of HotLoop Gateway; this is HotLoop IoT","product":"iot","feature":"reports"}
```

Not a 400, because there's no variable to set that fixes it, and not a 5xx,
because nothing went wrong. `GET /api/status` says up front which product
answered and which features it has, so a client can ask instead of probing.

### Everything that changes something is logged

Every create, change, delete, write, acknowledgement and login lands in the
system log (`GET /api/events`) with the user's name on it, and every write to a
tag, refused or not, lands in the write audit (`GET /api/writes`). The API does
not have a quiet path.

## Permissions

Who holds what. An account with an explicit permission list holds exactly what
it names instead of its role's set. `*` grants everything and `resource.*`
grants everything under a resource (`reports.*`). The admin role is `*`.

| Permission | viewer | operator | admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `devices.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `devices.write` | no | no | yes |
| `tags.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `tags.write` | no | no | yes |
| `values.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `values.write` | no | yes | yes |
| `board.write` | no | yes | yes |
| `entities.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `entities.write` | no | no | yes |
| `helpers.write` | no | yes | yes |
| `equipment.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `equipment.write` | no | no | yes |
| `alarms.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `alarms.write` | no | no | yes |
| `alarms.ack` | no | yes | yes |
| `automations.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `automations.write` | no | no | yes |
| `automations.trigger` | no | yes | yes |
| `scripts.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `scripts.run` | no | yes | yes |
| `scripts.write` | no | no | yes |
| `recipes.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `recipes.apply` | no | yes | yes |
| `recipes.write` | no | no | yes |
| `blueprints.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `blueprints.apply` | no | yes | yes |
| `blueprints.write` | no | no | yes |
| `dashboards.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `dashboards.write` | no | no | yes |
| `fleet.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `fleet.write` | no | yes | yes |
| `fleet.rebirth` | no | yes | yes |
| `fleet.restart` | no | no | yes |
| `fleet.update` | no | no | yes |
| `fleet.config` | no | no | yes |
| `notify.test` | no | no | yes |
| `notify.escalation` | no | no | yes |
| `backup.read` | no | no | yes |
| `backup.run` | no | no | yes |
| `reports.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `reports.run` | no | yes | yes |
| `reports.write` | no | no | yes |
| `sites.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `settings.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `settings.write` | no | no | yes |
| `events.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `logbook.read` | yes | yes | yes |
| `users.manage` | no | no | yes |

The line is the same everywhere: an operator runs the plant (writes values,
acknowledges alarms, triggers automations, nudges a relay), and only an admin
changes what the plant is configured to be, or does something to the outside
world on the Gateway's behalf (restarting a relay, pushing its config, sending
a test page, defining a report that emails plant data somewhere). Why each one
sits where it does is in the route comments in `internal/api/api.go` and in
[AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/#roles).

## Endpoint index

The permission column says what the route checks. `session` means any
logged-in user, with no permission beyond that. `none` means no session either,
and the section says why. `(in handler)` means the check is made inside the
handler rather than in front of it, and the section says why.

The product column says the smallest HotLoop that has the route: `all` is IoT,
Edge and Gateway, `edge` is Edge and Gateway, `gateway` is the Gateway alone.
Every product registers every route, and checks the same permission on it. On
a product that doesn't have it, the route answers 404 and says where it lives;
see [Not in this product](#not-in-this-product).

## Health

For the kubelet and load balancers. Neither needs a session: a probe has no
account, and neither says anything about the plant.

### `GET /healthz`

Liveness. `200` with the text `ok` as long as the process is serving HTTP.
It does not touch the database, on purpose: a database outage should take the
pod out of rotation, not get it restarted in a loop.

### `GET /readyz`

Readiness. Pings the database with a 5 second budget.

```json
{"status":"ready"}
```

`503` when it cannot reach it, with the reason in `detail` (the shape, from the
handler; the reason text is whatever the database driver said):

```json
{"error":"not ready","detail":"<why the database did not answer>"}
```

An app that cannot reach its historian should not be taking traffic.

## Authentication

See [AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/) for accounts, roles and the first admin.

### `POST /api/auth/login`

No session needed, by construction.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | Required. Case and surrounding spaces are ignored |
| `password` | string | Required |

```json
{"expiresAt":"2026-09-28T08:21:00.571794Z","permissions":["*"],"role":"admin","token":"<token>","username":"admin"}
```

Also sets the `iiot_session` cookie to the same token. `401`
`"invalid username or password"` for a wrong name, a wrong password or a
disabled account alike, and it takes as long either way: which of the three it
was is not something to tell a stranger. `429` for an account that has had too
many wrong passwords or PINs in a row, whatever is sent, with a `Retry-After`
header; see [AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/#the-lockout-after-wrong-passwords-and-pins).

### `POST /api/auth/kiosk`

Sign in at a shared panel with a PIN or a badge, the way
[AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/#kiosk-panels-pin-or-badge-and-an-idle-sign-out) describes. No
session needed, by construction.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | Required. The PIN, or the value a keyboard-wedge badge reader typed. Surrounding spaces are ignored |
| `username` | string | Optional. With it, only that account's PIN is checked and a wrong one counts toward that account's lockout. Without it, the code is looked for among every account's |

```json
{"expiresAt":"2026-10-21T08:21:00.571794Z","idleSec":300,"permissions":["status.read","tags.read"],"role":"operator","username":"olga"}
```

Sets the `iiot_session` cookie and, unlike `POST /api/auth/login`, does not
answer with the token: a kiosk session belongs to the browser at the panel.
`idleSec` is how long the session survives with nobody touching it. `401`
`"that PIN or badge isn't recognized"` for a wrong code, a code that is too short
and a disabled account's code alike, and it takes as long either way. `429` when the account is locked
(see [The lockout](/iot/authentication/#the-lockout-after-wrong-passwords-and-pins)), with a
`Retry-After` header. A code sent without a `username` that matches nobody is
not counted against any account; the panel that sent it, by client address, waits
half a second longer before its next such try is checked, up to
`ui.panelDelaySeconds`, and a right one starts it over. The panel is never locked. `400` when
the deployment runs with no login (`HOTLOOP_AUTH_INSECURE`), since there is then
nobody to sign in as.

### `POST /api/auth/activity`

A person touched the panel. No body. `{"status":"ok"}`. On a kiosk session this
is what moves its idle limit on; so is every other request that is not a read (a
write, an acknowledge). A `GET`, the live feed and the page's own background
loads are not: they would otherwise keep the last person signed in for ever. A
session made with a password has no idle limit and nothing to move.

### `POST /api/auth/logout`

Ends the session the request came with (cookie or bearer) and clears the
cookie. No body. `{"status":"logged out"}`.

### `GET /api/auth/session`

Who am I. For the UI's boot sequence.

```json
{"authenticated":true,"permissions":["*"],"role":"admin","username":"admin"}
```

A session made at a kiosk panel adds `"idleSec"`, its idle limit in seconds, which
is how the page knows to sign itself out.

With auth switched off (`HOTLOOP_AUTH_INSECURE`), it answers
`{"authenticated":false,"insecure":true}` instead of a 401, so the UI can say
why there is no login rather than guess.

### `POST /api/auth/password`

Change your own password. No permission: knowing your current password is the
credential.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `currentPassword` | string | Required |
| `newPassword` | string | Required, at least 8 characters |

`{"status":"password changed; log in again"}`. **Every session the account
holds ends, including this one**, and the cookie is cleared: a password change
that leaves the old sessions working is a change in name only. `401` if the
current password is wrong, `400` if the new one is too short.

## Users

All admin-only (`users.manage`). Password hashes never appear in a response;
the field has no JSON name.

### `GET /api/users`

```json
[{"username":"admin","role":"admin","disabled":false,"hasPin":false,"locked":false,"createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:19:28.036228Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:19:28.036228Z","lastLogin":"2026-09-27T20:21:00.575455Z"}]
```

`permissions` appears only on an account that has an explicit list. `hasPin` says
whether the account has a kiosk PIN or badge; the value and its hash never appear.

### `POST /api/users`

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | Required. Lowercase letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen, starting with a letter or digit, 2 to 64 characters |
| `password` | string | Required, at least 8 characters |
| `role` | string | `admin`, `operator` or `viewer`. Defaults to `viewer` |
| `permissions` | string[] | Optional. Replaces the role's set entirely |

Answers the new user. `400` for a bad name, role or password, `409` if the name
is taken.

### `PUT /api/users/{username}`

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | string | Required unless `permissions` is set |
| `permissions` | string[] | Optional. Empty means "use the role" |
| `disabled` | bool | `true` disables the account and ends every session it holds |

Answers the updated user. `400` for an unknown role, or for disabling the last
enabled admin: that is a lockout with nobody left to undo it. `404` for an
unknown user.

### `DELETE /api/users/{username}`

`{"status":"deleted"}`. `400` for your own account or the last enabled admin,
`404` for an unknown user.

### `POST /api/users/{username}/password`

An admin sets somebody else's password without knowing the old one.
`{"password": "..."}`, at least 8 characters. Answers
`{"status":"password reset"}` and ends every session that account holds.

### `PUT /api/users/{username}/pin`

An admin gives an account a PIN or badge value for signing in at a kiosk panel,
or replaces the one it has. `{"code": "482913"}`: 6 to 72 characters, no spaces
or control characters, digits or anything else a badge reader types. Answers
`{"status":"PIN set","username":"olga","hasPin":true}`. The value is hashed with
bcrypt, as a password is, and is never logged or sent back. `400` for a code that
is too short, too long or has a space in it, and for a code another account
already has: a panel finds the account by the code alone, so one code opens one
account. `404` for an unknown user. It does not touch the password or any
session.

### `DELETE /api/users/{username}/lockout`

Lets a locked account back in before its lock runs out, and starts its count of
wrong passwords and PINs from zero. `{"status":"unlocked","username":"olga","locked":false}`.
`404` for an unknown user. A locked account shows `"locked":true` and
`"lockedUntil"` in `GET /api/users`.

### `DELETE /api/users/{username}/pin`

Takes the PIN or badge away and signs the account out of every kiosk panel it is
signed in at. Its password, and its sessions on its own computer, are untouched.
`{"status":"PIN cleared","username":"olga","hasPin":false}`. `404` for an unknown
user.

## Status and diagnostics

### `GET /api/status`

The header bar: runtime counters, the alarm summary, the plant's name, and
which product this is. `product` is `iot`, `edge` or `gateway`, the same as
`hotloop --product`. `features` is which of the features that differ between
products this one has: `edge-publish`, `fleet`, `opcua-server`, `reports` and
`sites` in a Gateway, the first and third in Edge, none in IoT. `version` is the
build, and `imageDigest` is the digest of the image it was started from, which
a version number can't tell you on a box that follows `:stable`. It is there
only when the supervisor said (the Quadlet units do, before every start; a bare
binary and a Helm install can't) and is left out otherwise.

```json
{
  "alarms": {"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0,"unacked":0,"total":1},
  "features": ["edge-publish","fleet","opcua-server","reports","sites"],
  "plantName": "Demo Plant",
  "product": "gateway",
  "runtime": {
    "startedAt": "2026-09-27T20:19:28.06635851Z", "uptime": "11m13s",
    "devices": 2, "connected": 2, "degraded": 0, "disconnected": 0,
    "tags": 5, "cachedTags": 5, "writesOk": 4, "writesRefused": 3,
    "bus": {"subscribers":4,"published":653,"dropped":0},
    "historian": {"queued":1085,"written":1085,"filtered":329,"dropped":0,"failed":0,"queueLen":0,"queueCap":50000},
    "writePolicy": {"allowWrites":true,"allowMcpWrites":false,"confirmWrites":true},
    "protocols": ["ethernet-ip","http","modbus","mqtt","mtconnect","opcua","s7comm","snmp","unifi"]
  },
  "siteId": "docs",
  "version": "4.18.11"
}
```

### `GET /api/protocols`

Every protocol the Gateway knows, and whether this build has its driver.

```json
[{"id":"opcua","name":"OPC UA","description":"The universal one. ...","transport":"opc.tcp binary","defaultPort":4840,"writable":true,"browsable":true,"deviceTypes":["plc","cnc","robot","ipc","hmi","historian","gateway"],"library":"github.com/gopcua/opcua","available":true}]
```

### `GET /api/diagnostics`

What the diagnostics screen shows: database pool, historian queue and
history size, the tag bus, the entity engine, the logbook's recorder, the
runtime, MCP (server and outbound connections) and the automation engine's
armed rules, webhook paths and state-change queue.

```json
{
  "automations": {"armed":[],"stateChangesDropped":0,"stateChangesPending":0,"webhooks":[]},
  "bus": {"subscribers":4,"published":654,"dropped":0},
  "database": {"type":"postgres","totalConns":3,"idleConns":3,"acquiredConns":0,"maxConns":10,"historyMode":"timescale","timescaleVersion":"2.30.1"},
  "entities": {"entities":8,"droppedBatches":0,"pendingChanges":0,"droppedChanges":0},
  "historian": {"queued":1087,"written":1085,"filtered":329,"dropped":0,"failed":0,"queueLen":0,"queueCap":50000},
  "historyStats": {"mode":"timescale","rows":996,"distinctTags":5,"oldest":"2026-09-27T20:21:38.609853Z","newest":"2026-09-27T20:30:39.507987Z","sizeBytes":73728},
  "logbook": {"recording":true,"retentionDays":90,"queued":0,"dropped":0,"written":212,"suppressed":36,"writeErrors":0},
  "mcp": {"outbound":[],"path":"/mcp","serverEnabled":true,"tokenSet":true},
  "runtime": {"...": "the same block as /api/status"}
}
```

With outbound MCP servers configured, `outbound` lists each one:

```json
{"name":"plant-a","target":"http://localhost:8080/mcp","connected":true,"tools":["ack_alarm","call_service","...","write_tag"],"connectedSince":"2026-09-27T20:45:50Z"}
```

Any credential in an outbound server's `target` or `lastError` is scrubbed,
because a URL or a command line can carry a token and every role can read
this. The MCP token itself is only ever `tokenSet`.

## Devices

A device is one connection over one protocol. What goes in `config` and
`address` depends on the protocol: see [PROTOCOLS.md](/iot/protocols/).

### `GET /api/devices`

Every device, with its live connection state. Credentials are `[redacted]`.

```json
[{"id":"tank-farm","name":"Tank farm","protocol":"mqtt","address":"base-mqtt:1883","enabled":true,
  "site":"Demo Plant","area":"Utilities","equipmentId":4,
  "config":{"clientId":"docs-api-tankfarm","password":"[redacted]","topics":["docs-api-example/#"],"username":"tank","writeTopic":"docs-api-example/{tag}/set"},
  "createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:21:01.637319Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:21:01.637319Z",
  "state":"connected","lastPoll":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.412Z",
  "latencyMs":0.002,"tagCount":3,"pollCount":1}]
```

`state` is `connected`, `connecting`, `degraded` (up, but polls failing),
`disconnected` or `disabled`. `lastError`, `errorCount` and the rest appear
when there is something to say.

### `POST /api/devices`

Creates the device if the `id` is new, replaces it if not. There is no `PUT`.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Required. 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, starting alphanumeric. It ends up in URLs, MQTT topics and MCP arguments |
| `name` | string | Required |
| `protocol` | string | Required. One this build has a driver for (`GET /api/protocols`) |
| `address` | string | Required. Host and port, an `opc.tcp://` or `http://` URL: the protocol decides |
| `enabled` | bool | Left out is `false` |
| `description` | string | |
| `pollIntervalMs`, `timeoutMs` | int | 0 takes the runtime default. The poll interval is floored at `HOTLOOP_MIN_POLL_INTERVAL` |
| `site`, `area`, `line` | string | Places the device on the equipment tree by name, creating nodes as needed |
| `equipmentId` | int | Places it on a tree node instead; `site`, `area` and `line` then come from the node. See [EQUIPMENT.md](/iot/equipment/) |
| `config` | object | The protocol's own options. Credentials follow the [write-only rules](#secrets-are-write-only) |

Runtime fields (`state`, `lastPoll`, `tagCount` and so on) are read-only;
send them back and they are ignored. Answers the saved device, redacted. `400`
for a protocol with no driver, a failed validation or a credential rule; the
runtime reloads with it straight away.

```json
{"error":"no driver for protocol \"profibus\"; this build speaks: ethernet-ip, http, modbus, mqtt, mtconnect, opcua, s7comm, snmp, unifi"}
```

### `GET /api/devices/{id}`

The device, its tags and its labels.

```json
{"device":{"id":"tank-farm","name":"Tank farm","...":"..."},"labels":["critical"],"tags":[{"id":3,"deviceId":"tank-farm","name":"level","...":"..."}]}
```

`tags` is `[]` for a device with none. `404` for an unknown id.

### `DELETE /api/devices/{id}`

Deletes the device, its tags and their entities. **Its history is kept.**
`{"deleted":"tank-farm"}`, or `404`.

### `POST /api/devices/{id}/enabled`

`{"enabled": false}` stops polling without deleting anything. Answers
`{"enabled":false,"id":"tank-farm"}`. `404` for an unknown id.

### `POST /api/devices/{id}/browse`

Asks the device what points it has. Needs only `devices.read`, because it
reads. No body.

```json
{"supported":true,"tags":[{"name":"Plant_Boiler_Temperature","address":"nsu=http://plant/;s=Temperature","dataType":"float","description":"Temperature","writable":true}]}
```

A protocol that cannot enumerate its points (Modbus, S7comm, HTTP) answers
`200` with `{"supported":false,"reason":"..."}`: that is a fact about the
protocol, not an error. `503` if the device is not connected. `writable` here
is what the device says about the point, not whether the Gateway will write
it.

### `POST /api/devices/{id}/import`

Turns browse results into configured tags. Needs `tags.write`, because it
creates tags.

```json
{"tags":[{"name":"Temperature","address":"nsu=http://emberburn/;s=Temperature","dataType":"float","unit":"C"}]}
```

Each entry takes `name`, `address`, `dataType`, `unit`, `description`,
`deviceClass` and `writable` (the browse result as it came). Answers
`{"inserted":2,"updated":0}`. **Every imported tag is read-only**, whatever
the device said: a discovered point is not a point anybody has decided may be
commanded, and defaulting the other way would arm a few thousand of them at
once. Arm the ones you mean with `POST /api/tags`. `404` for an unknown device.

## UniFi: OT networks, clients, and where a device is on the network

HotLoop's own record about UniFi sites. See [UNIFI.md](/iot/unifi/). `{id}` under
`/api/unifi` is a UniFi device (one site on one console); `{network}` is the
console's own ID for a network, as `GET .../networks` gives it; `{mac}` takes
any usual spelling and is kept lower case with colons.

**None of these ask the console anything.** They read the driver's last read
of it, so a screen left open costs the console nothing. That also means they
answer `503` until the device has been read once, and always in an
`--mcp-stdio` helper, which never logs in to a console. None of them writes to
a console either.

A change that makes or removes an alarm says so in `change`:
`{"alarmsCreated":["unifi-unknown-3f2a9c01b7de"]}`. Those are ordinary alarm
definitions, under `/api/alarms`.

### `GET /api/devices/{id}/network`

Where a HotLoop device (a PLC, a meter) is on the network. Linked:

```json
{"deviceId":"plc-07","link":{"deviceId":"plc-07","consoleId":"plant-net","mac":"02:48:4c:00:00:07","confirmedBy":"hana","confirmedAt":"2026-09-28T18:02:05Z"},
 "consoleName":"Plant network","client":{"mac":"02:48:4c:00:00:07","ip":"10.77.0.7","switchMac":"00:27:22:e2:1d:6f","switchName":"USW Lite 8 PoE","port":5,"portUp":false,"online":false,"lastSeen":"2026-09-28T18:01:40Z","lastSeenSec":25,"why":"its switch port 5 has no link","...":"..."},
 "readAt":"2026-09-28T18:02:05Z","summary":"on USW Lite 8 PoE port 5, link down; the console last saw it 25s ago; off the network: its switch port 5 has no link","proposals":[]}
```

Not linked, `link` is `null` and `proposals` lists the clients any console
HotLoop reads has at the device's IP, newest first. A proposal is only that:
the console's IPs lag, so nothing is linked until an admin confirms one.

### `PUT /api/devices/{id}/network`

`{"consoleId":"plant-net","mac":"02:48:4c:00:00:07"}` confirms which client the
device is. From then on the MAC is the key and the IP is never trusted again.
The client gets tags (`c.<mac>.*` on the console) and an alarm, "PLC-07 off the
network", priority 1 with a 120 s on-delay so a reboot doesn't page anybody.
Answers `{"link":{...},"change":{...}}`. `400` if `consoleId` isn't a UniFi
device or the MAC isn't one, `404` for an unknown device.

### `DELETE /api/devices/{id}/network`

Removes the link, and the alarm HotLoop made for it unless the client is still
watched from a known list. `404` if there was no link.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/networks`

The site's networks as the console has them, with HotLoop's record: `ot`,
`known` (how many devices are on its list), `clients` (on it now) and
`unknown` (on it now and not on the list). A network HotLoop has a record of
that the console no longer has comes back with `"onConsole":false`.

```json
[{"networkId":"6abb23d25a95f2636a5df29c","name":"SCADA","purpose":"corporate","vlan":122,"subnet":"10.122.0.1/24","onConsole":true,"ot":true,"clients":2,"known":1,"unknown":[{"mac":"02:9b:b1:69:88:f2","ip":"10.122.0.66","switchName":"USW Lite 8 PoE","port":6,"...":"..."}],"changedBy":"hana"}]
```

### `PUT /api/unifi/{id}/networks/{network}`

`{"ot": true}` marks a network OT. Anything on it that isn't on its known list
counts in `n.<network>.unknown` and names itself in `.unknown_last`, and HotLoop
makes the alarm "Unknown device on SCADA", priority 1. `{"ot": false}` unmarks
it and removes that alarm; the known list is kept. `400` for a WAN or a network
the console doesn't have.

### `POST /api/unifi/{id}/networks/{network}/accept-all`

Accepts everything on the network now, as it is: the one click after marking
it. Devices already on the list keep their name and watch. No body. Answers
`{"accepted":[{known device}...]}`, the ones it added.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/known`

Every known device on the site's networks:
`[{"deviceId":"plant-net","networkId":"...","mac":"...","name":"PLC-07","watch":true,"acceptedBy":"hana","acceptedAt":"..."}]`.

### `PUT /api/unifi/{id}/networks/{network}/known/{mac}`

`{"name":"PLC-07","watch":true}` accepts a device onto the network, or changes
its name or watch. `watch` gives it tags and the offline alarm; a device that's
allowed on but comes and goes (a maintenance laptop) is accepted without it.
`400` if the network was never marked OT.

### `DELETE /api/unifi/{id}/networks/{network}/known/{mac}`

Takes a device off the list. If it's on the network, it's unknown again on the
next read.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/clients`

Every client the console lists, plus every watched one it doesn't, each with
where it is, whether it's online, and `ot`, `known`, `watched`, `linkedTo`
and a one-line `summary`. `?q=` narrows it to a MAC, IP or name.

### `GET /api/unifi/consoles`

Every UniFi device HotLoop has, running or not, for the UniFi screen's picker:
`[{"id":"plant-net","name":"Plant network","address":"https://...","enabled":true,"running":true,"site":"default","version":"10.6.106","readAt":"...","devices":4,"online":4,"clients":12,"failover":false,"eventsLive":true}]`.
A console this process hasn't read says why in `why`.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/overview`

The Overview card: device and client counts (a client counts when HotLoop
believes it is on the network, the test the `n.<id>.clients` tags use, not
merely when the console lists it), clients per network, the console's subsystem
`health`, and for each gateway its WAN strip, `gateways[]`: one `wans[]` entry
per WAN with `alive` (the gateway's own health checks, never the WAN block's
`up`), `known`, `active`, `backup`, latency and availability. `failover` is
traffic on a WAN that isn't the first, `down` is no WAN alive, and `since` is
the first read HotLoop saw traffic on the WAN it is on now, which is when
HotLoop noticed, not when the gateway moved. `events` is the state of the
events websocket (`live`, `error`, `reconnects`) and the newest ten events.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/topology`

The map. `nodes[]` are the adopted devices with their place on the grid (`x`,
`y`, `layer`: left to right from the gateway, laid out the same way for the
same read), `edges[]` the cables between them from the console's own
`downlink_table`, `wired[]` and `wifi[]` the clients hanging off each switch
port and each AP and SSID. A device nothing lists as plugged into anything is
drawn on its own with `noUplink` set, not hung off the gateway on a guess. A
device of another UniFi console HotLoop reads that this console lists as a
client is stitched in as a node with `external` set and an edge with
`stitched`. `feeds` is, by device MAC, the HotLoop devices linked to a client
downstream of it, with their `equipmentId` for the Plant tree, and `links`
those same devices by client MAC.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/devices`

Every adopted device with its numbers and its `ports[]` for the faceplate:
link, speed, PoE mode and draw, the clients learned on the port, the device
plugged into it, and `dropped` for a port that was up at an earlier read and is
down now. A device the console has lost reports no numbers and no port links,
because what it said last isn't current.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/wifi`

The site's SSIDs with `enabled`, the network they sit on and how many clients
are on each. When the console won't show this account its wireless networks,
`error` says why and `wlans` is empty.

### `GET /api/unifi/{id}/events`

The newest events the console has reported since HotLoop connected, newest
first (`?limit=` up to 200, default 50), and the state of the events websocket.
Each event has the controller's `key` (`EVT_SW_Lost_Contact`), its own `message`,
`severity` (`warning` when the controller flags it as something going wrong) and
the device, client and port it is about. They are also in the logbook, filed
under the switch or access point they are about (see
[UNIFI.md](/iot/unifi/#events)).

### `POST /api/unifi/{id}/starter-alarms`

Makes the usual alarms for the site from what the console has now, as ordinary
alarm definitions under `/api/alarms`: every adopted device offline (priority 2,
60 s on-delay), every uplink port down (priority 1, 10 s), a gateway with two
or more WANs running on a backup one (priority 2, 30 s). The body is optional.
`{"poeLimitW": 25}` adds a priority 3 alarm on every PoE port's `poe_w` draw
over that many watts, 30 s on-delay; the console doesn't say what a port's
budget is, so HotLoop doesn't guess one. A negative limit is a `400`.

```json
{"created":[{"id":"unifi-devoffline-9c1e2a77b3d0","name":"USW Lite 8 PoE offline","kind":"offline","tag":"d.002722e2e633.online","priority":2}],
 "kept":[]}
```

`kept` are alarms the set calls for that were already there: its own from an
earlier press, or someone's own alarm on the same tag. So it is safe to press
again after adopting more gear, and it only adds the new gear. The OT-network
and off-the-network alarms are not part of it; they come with marking a
network OT and watching a device. `503` until the console has been read once.

## MQTT discovery

Devices that announced themselves over MQTT, and what a person decided about
each. See [DISCOVERY.md](/iot/mqtt-discovery/). Discovery listens on the embedded
broker when it runs, and on every broker set up under `/api/mqtt/brokers`. With
neither, `sources` is empty. In an `--mcp-stdio` helper, which never listens,
`GET /api/discovery` answers `{"running":false,"sources":[],"devices":[]}` and
every other route `503`.

`{source}` is the broker a device announced on (`embedded` for HotLoop's own,
otherwise the broker's id);
`{key}` is what tied its announcements together: its first identifier, its MAC
as `mac:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`, or its node id. URL-encode it; identifiers carry
characters a path doesn't.

**None of these arm anything.** Accepting a device makes its points armable,
one at a time, through `POST /api/tags` like every other point.

### `GET /api/discovery`

Every source, with what it has seen and refused, and every discovered device:

```json
{"running":true,"sources":[{"id":"embedded","name":"the embedded broker","prefix":"homeassistant","listening":true,"connected":true,
  "received":42,"dropped":0,"refused":0,"problems":[],"autoCreate":true,"anonymousAllowed":false,
  "external":false,"listenOnly":false,"enabled":true}],
 "devices":[{"source":"embedded","deviceKey":"plug-0001","deviceId":"kitchen-plug","status":"discovered",
  "device":{"identifiers":["plug-0001"],"name":"Kitchen Plug","manufacturer":"Acme","model":"P1","swVersion":"1.0.0"},
  "origin":{"name":"test-publisher","swVersion":"0.1"},"firstSeen":"2026-10-02T09:12:04Z","lastSeen":"2026-10-02T09:12:04Z",
  "components":[{"key":"plug-0001-relay","component":"switch","name":"Relay","configTopic":"homeassistant/switch/plug-0001/relay/config",
   "stateTopic":"plug/relay","commandTopic":"plug/relay/set","commandTopics":["plug/relay/set"],"tag":"relay",
   "unsupported":[],"unknownKeys":[],"flags":[]}]}]}
```

A source with `external` true is a broker set up under `/api/mqtt/brokers`,
and `broker` says where it is. `autoCreate` false is a source whose devices
wait in the inbox: listed `discovered` with no `deviceId`, nothing made and
nothing reading until somebody accepts one. `listenOnly` is a broker HotLoop
never publishes on. `lastError` says why a source isn't connected, a password
that can't be opened included.

`status` is `discovered`, `accepted` or `ignored`. Per component,
`unsupported` lists what HotLoop can't use and why ("value template not
supported: filter `regex_findall_index` is not supported at column 12"),
`unknownKeys` the config keys the format doesn't define, `commandTopics` every
topic its commands can go to (a fan's speed topic as well as its main one),
and `flags` what a person should look at before accepting: a command topic
outside the topics the component reads, inside the discovery prefix, or
claimed by another device,
and a config that asks for retained commands. `withdrawnAt` is set on a
component the publisher withdrew. `suggestedEquipmentId` is the tree node the
device's `suggested_area` names, when exactly one node has that name; it only
pre-fills the accept dialog. On the embedded broker, `announcedBy` and
`announcedVia` are the broker login and client id that published its latest
config, and `acceptedLogin` the login it was accepted from. An accepted device
whose announcement changed, or that a different login announced, has `review`:

```json
{"hash":"9a1c...","summary":["plug-0001-power: unit changed"],
 "changes":[{"key":"plug-0001-power","kind":"changed","fields":[{"field":"unit","running":"W","announced":"kW"}]}]}
```

### `GET /api/discovery/{source}/{key}`

One device, the same shape. `404` for one HotLoop hasn't seen.

### `POST /api/discovery/{source}/{key}/accept`

Accepts a device. Optional body `{"equipmentId": 12}` places it on the tree in
the same step. Arms nothing. Answers the device. `400` for an ignored one.

### `POST /api/discovery/{source}/{key}/ignore`

Drops the device: its HotLoop device, tags and entities go (its history
stays), and it stays ignored when it announces again. Answers the device.
`DELETE /api/devices/{id}` on a discovered device does the same, because a
device that keeps announcing would just come back.

### `POST /api/discovery/{source}/{key}/unignore`

Brings an ignored device back as discovered, from what it last announced.
`400` if it isn't ignored.

### `POST /api/discovery/{source}/{key}/review/apply`

Makes an accepted device run what it announced. Whether each point is armed
stays as it was. `400` when nothing is waiting for review.

### `POST /api/discovery/{source}/{key}/review/reject`

Keeps the accepted config running and stops offering this change. A
different change later is offered again. `400` when nothing is waiting.

A review can be about who announced it: a change with `"kind":"publisher"`
and the summary line "announced by login garage-node; accepted from
kitchen-node". Applying it makes that login the one the device is accepted
from.

## Broker logins

The embedded broker's logins made in HotLoop, each with the topics it may
publish and subscribe to. See [BROKER.md](/iot/broker/). A login is a key to the
whole plant's broker, so these are `users.manage`, an admin's. Nothing here
ever answers with a password or its hash. Each change goes on the log and holds
from the client's next publish; nobody has to reconnect.

### `GET /api/broker/logins`

```json
{"running":true,"anonymous":false,"prefix":"homeassistant","envLogins":["plant"],
 "profiles":[{"name":"shelly","about":"a Shelly Gen2 or later; name the login after its MQTT topic prefix",
   "publish":["%u/#","shellies/announce"],"subscribe":["%u/#","shellies/command","%p/status"]}],
 "logins":[{"name":"kitchen-node","profile":"esphome","publish":["%u/#","%p/+/%u/+/config","esphome/discover/%u"],
   "subscribe":["%u/#","%p/status","esphome/discover"],"createdBy":"admin","createdAt":"2026-10-02T09:12:04Z",
   "updatedAt":"2026-10-02T09:12:04Z","resolvedPublish":["kitchen-node/#","homeassistant/+/kitchen-node/+/config",
   "esphome/discover/kitchen-node"],"resolvedSubscribe":["kitchen-node/#","homeassistant/status","esphome/discover"]}]}
```

`running` is false where this process doesn't run the broker; the logins are
still kept, and the broker reads them when it starts. `envLogins` are the names
from `HOTLOOP_BROKER_USERS`, which can do anything. `%u` in a rule is the
login's own name and `%p` the discovery prefix; `resolved*` are the rules with
both filled in.

### `POST /api/broker/logins`

```json
{"name":"kitchen-node","password":"a-long-random-password","profile":"esphome"}
```

`name` is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-` and `_` (it stands for `%u` in topics).
`password` is at least 12 characters. `profile` fills in the rules; `publish`
and `subscribe`, when given, replace them. One of the two is needed. A rule is
an MQTT topic filter: `+` and `#` only as whole levels, `#` only last, never a
`$` topic. `201` with the login; `400` for any of the above or a name
`HOTLOOP_BROKER_USERS` already has; `409` for a name that's taken.

### `PUT /api/broker/logins/{name}`

Any of `profile`, `publish`, `subscribe` and `password`; what isn't sent stays.
`200` with the login, `404` for one that doesn't exist.

### `DELETE /api/broker/logins/{name}`

`200` `{"deleted":"kitchen-node"}`. A client still connected with it can do
nothing from then on, and it can't connect again. `404` for one that doesn't
exist.

## Network discovery

Devices heard on the plant network over mDNS, SSDP and DHCP, and what a
person decided about each. See [NETWORK-DISCOVERY.md](/iot/network-discovery/).
In an `--mcp-stdio` helper, which never listens, `GET /api/network-discovery`
answers `{"running":false,"finds":[]}` and every other route `503`.

`{key}` is how a find was heard and who by: `mdns:` and its mDNS host name,
`ssdp:` and its UPnP uuid, `dhcp:` and its MAC. URL-encode it.

**None of these arm anything**, and nothing here is added until somebody
accepts it.

### `GET /api/network-discovery`

The listeners, probing, the interfaces they're on, and every find:

```json
{"running":true,
 "status":{"leading":true,"interfaces":["eth0 10.20.0.15/24"],
  "listeners":[{"name":"mdns","enabled":true,"listening":true,"heard":120,"dropped":0,"refused":0},
   {"name":"ssdp","enabled":true,"listening":true,"heard":14,"dropped":0,"refused":0},
   {"name":"dhcp","enabled":false,"listening":false,"heard":0,"dropped":0,"refused":0}],
  "probe":{"networks":[]}},
 "finds":[{"key":"mdns:line3-ua.local","via":"mdns","kind":"opcua","name":"line3-ua","status":"discovered",
  "firstSeen":"2026-10-11T14:02:11Z","lastSeen":"2026-10-11T14:07:40Z",
  "find":{"key":"mdns:line3-ua.local","via":"mdns","kind":"opcua","name":"line3-ua",
   "summary":"OPC UA server, capabilities DA","host":"line3-ua.local","addresses":["10.20.0.31"],
   "services":[{"type":"_opcua-tcp._tcp.local","instance":"line3-ua._opcua-tcp._tcp.local","port":50000,
    "txt":{"caps":"DA","path":"/"}}],
   "proposal":{"protocol":"opcua","address":"opc.tcp://10.20.0.31:50000/","how":"Accepting makes an OPC UA device..."},
   "heard":"2026-10-11T14:07:40Z"}}]}
```

`kind` is `esphome`, `shelly`, `opcua`, `mqtt-broker`, `web`, `mdns` (it
announced something HotLoop has no word for), `upnp` or `dhcp`. A find whose
`proposal` has a `protocol` becomes a device of that protocol at `address`
when accepted; one without says in `how` what would bring it in. `also` lists
the other finds and MQTT-discovered devices that are the same box, by MAC or
address. `status` is `discovered`, `accepted` or `ignored`, and `deviceId` the
device accepting made. A listener's `error` says why it isn't listening (port
67 taken or not allowed, no multicast interface); `refused` counts new finds
dropped because the record is full.

### `GET /api/network-discovery/{key}`

One find, the same shape. `404` for one HotLoop hasn't heard.

### `POST /api/network-discovery/{key}/accept`

Accepts a find. Optional body `{"equipmentId": 12}` places the device it makes
on the tree. A find HotLoop has a driver for becomes a device at the proposed
address, enabled, with no tags and nothing armed; any other is recorded as
known and makes nothing. Answers the find. `400` for one that's accepted or
ignored already.

### `POST /api/network-discovery/{key}/ignore`

Hides a find nobody has decided about, and keeps it hidden when it's heard
again. `400` for one that's been decided.

### `POST /api/network-discovery/{key}/unignore`

Brings an ignored find back to be decided about. `400` if it isn't ignored.

### `POST /api/network-discovery/probe`

Probes now: an mDNS query and an SSDP search on every interface whose network
is listed in `HOTLOOP_NETDISC_PROBE_NETWORKS`, and nowhere else. Answers
`{"status": ...}`, with what didn't go out in `status.probe.lastError`. `400`
when no network has probing switched on: this button can't switch it on, only
the deployment can.

## Integrations

The config flow for a kind of device a person points HotLoop at: ask what the
integration needs, look at the real device with the answers, and make the
device and its tags from what was found. See [INTEGRATIONS.md](/iot/integrations/).

**Nothing here arms anything.** Every tag a setup makes is read-only. Arming
one is `POST /api/tags` like every other point.

### `GET /api/integrations`

Every integration this build has, with the questions it asks:

```json
[{"id":"opcua","name":"OPC UA server","description":"A PLC, CNC, gateway or SCADA server ...",
  "protocol":"opcua","addressLabel":"Endpoint","addressPlaceholder":"opc.tcp://192.168.1.20:4840","writable":true,
  "fields":[{"key":"securityMode","label":"Security","kind":"choice","required":false,"default":"None",
             "choices":[{"value":"None","label":"None"},{"value":"Sign","label":"Sign"}]},
            {"key":"password","label":"Password","kind":"secret","required":false}]}]
```

`kind` is `text`, `number`, `bool`, `choice` or `secret`. A field with
`showWhen` (`{"version":["3"]}`) is only asked when another answer has one of
those values, and an answer to a question that is not showing is ignored.

### `POST /api/integrations/{id}/probe`

Checks the answers and goes and looks at the real device. Saves nothing.

```json
{"address":"opc.tcp://192.168.1.20:4840","options":{"securityMode":"None"}}
```

Answers `{"integration":"opcua","address":"opc.tcp://192.168.1.20:4840","found":{...}}`.
`address` is the address as the integration resolved it. `found` has `name`
(what the device calls itself), `identity` (what it says it is), `notes`
(things to know before accepting) and `points`, each a tag-shaped
`{name, address, dataType, unit, description, writable, deviceClass}` plus
`group`, `sample` (what it read when it was found) and `suggested`.

`400` for answers that don't fit the questions, all the problems at once; an
answer for a question the integration doesn't ask is a `400` too, not ignored.
`502` when the device didn't answer or answered with something that isn't its
protocol, with what went wrong. `404` for an integration this build doesn't
have. A secret is never in an answer or an error.

### `POST /api/integrations/{id}/setup`

Looks at the device again, then creates it and its tags. The body is the
probe's, plus:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `deviceId` | The new device's id. Blank takes one from the name. `400` if a device has it |
| `name` | The device's name. Blank takes what the device calls itself |
| `points` | Names from `found.points` to set up. Blank takes the ones marked `suggested`. A name the device doesn't have is a `400` |
| `site`, `area`, `line` | Where it goes on the equipment tree, as on `POST /api/devices` |

The points are checked against the device as it is now, not against what a
client says it found a minute ago. Answers `{"device":{...},"tags":3,"entities":["sensor.plc_sim_..."],"notes":[]}`.
The device is enabled and polling, every tag is read-only, and each tag has
its read entity. A setup that fails part way leaves no device behind.

## MQTT brokers

Brokers other than HotLoop's own that discovery listens to: a plant's
Mosquitto, the broker a Zigbee2MQTT box brought along. See
[DISCOVERY.md](/iot/mqtt-discovery/#other-brokers). Their passwords are sealed with the
device credential key (`HOTLOOP_SECRET_KEY_FILE`) and never answered with;
`passwordSet` says whether one is stored, and `passwordProblem` why a stored
one can't be opened. Every change goes on the log and takes effect at once:
the listener and the devices from that broker connect again.

### `GET /api/mqtt/brokers`

```json
{"secretKey":true,
 "brokers":[{"id":"plant-uns","name":"Plant UNS","broker":"tcp://10.20.0.5:1883","username":"hotloop","useTls":false,
   "insecureSkipVerify":false,"prefix":"homeassistant","listenOnly":true,"autoCreate":false,"tasmota":true,"shelly":true,"enabled":true,
   "createdBy":"admin","passwordSet":true,"createdAt":"2026-10-03T09:12:04Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-03T09:12:04Z"}]}
```

`secretKey` is whether this HotLoop has a key to seal a password with.

### `POST /api/mqtt/brokers`

```json
{"id":"plant-uns","name":"Plant UNS","broker":"tcp://10.20.0.5:1883","username":"hotloop",
 "password":"...","listenOnly":true}
```

`id` is 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and `-`, not `embedded`: it names the
broker in every device that came from it, and can't change. `broker` is
`host:port` or a `tcp://`, `ssl://`, `tls://`, `mqtt://` or `mqtts://`
URL, with no login in it. `prefix` defaults to `homeassistant`; `autoCreate`
to false (devices wait in the inbox); `listenOnly` to false; `tasmota` (hear
Tasmota's own discovery, `tasmota/discovery/#`, too) to true; `shelly` (learn
Shelly Gen2 and later devices from the `<prefix>/status/<component>` topics they
publish) to true; `enabled` to true.
A password needs a username, and a key: without `HOTLOOP_SECRET_KEY_FILE` it's
a `400`, never stored in the clear. `201` with the broker; `409` for an id
that's taken.

### `PUT /api/mqtt/brokers/{id}`

Any of the fields above but `id`; what isn't sent stays. `"password":""`
clears the password. `200` with the broker.

### `DELETE /api/mqtt/brokers/{id}`

Removes the broker and what it announced that nobody accepted: the inbox, and
any device it made on its own. `409` naming them while devices accepted from
it still exist: ignore or delete those first, or switch the broker off with
`"enabled":false` instead. `200` `{"deleted":"plant-uns"}`.

## Tags

### `GET /api/tags`

| Query | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| `device` | Every tag on one device. When set, `q` and `limit` are ignored |
| `q` | Search: a case-insensitive substring of the device id, tag name or description |
| `limit` | Default 500, at most 1000 |

```json
[{"id":5,"deviceId":"tank-farm","name":"level_sp","address":"mqtt:docs-api-example/level_sp","dataType":"float","unit":"%","enabled":true,"writable":true,"maxValue":95,"hasRange":true,"scale":1,"createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.405164Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.405164Z"}]
```

### `POST /api/tags`

Creates the tag if `deviceId` and `name` are new, replaces it if not.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `deviceId` | string | Required. The device must exist (`404` if not) |
| `name` | string | Required. No control characters |
| `address` | string | Required. The protocol's own address |
| `dataType` | string | `bool`, `int`, `float` or `string` (and the usual aliases: `int16`, `word`, `coil`...). Decides how a write is encoded |
| `unit`, `description` | string | |
| `enabled` | bool | Left out is `false` |
| `writable` | bool | **Arms the tag for writing, from every path: UI, automations, entities, MCP.** Left out is `false` |
| `hasRange`, `minValue`, `maxValue` | bool, number, number | With `hasRange`, a write outside the range is refused (never clamped) |
| `scale`, `offset` | number | engineering = raw x scale + offset. A scale of 0 is 1 |
| `noData` | list | Raw values that mean "no measurement", each `{"raw", "reason"}`. `raw` is a string (`"0x8005"`, `"-32763"`) or a bare number, and comes back as a string. A reading whose raw value is on the list is bad quality with that `reason`, checked before `scale` and `offset`. Up to 32 codes. A code that is not a whole number, is listed twice, or can't be the point's type is `400`. See [PROTOCOLS.md](/iot/protocols/#no-data-values) for what to write for each type and the Yokogawa DX example |
| `deadband`, `deadbandPercent` | number | Changes smaller than this are not written to history |
| `deviceClass` | string | The class the tag's entities start with (`power`, `connectivity`, `temperature`...), when it means something for their domain. Taken when the tag is created and ignored on a replace: from then on the entity owns its class, so change it there |

Answers the saved tag. Saving one with `writable: true` is logged as such: arming
a tag is a safety decision and gets a name against it. The tag's entities are
created or updated before the answer, so a client can ask for them straight
away.

A tag on a discovered device nobody has accepted can't be armed: `400`,
"accept the device first". See [DISCOVERY.md](/iot/mqtt-discovery/#commands).

### `DELETE /api/tags/{device}/{name}`

`{"deleted":"tank-farm/level"}`, or `404`. The history stays. The tag's
entities become orphans (see [ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/#deleted-tags-orphans-and-re-adoption)).

## Values, the board, and writes

### `GET /api/values`

The latest reading of every tag, from memory. `?device=` narrows it to one
device.

```json
[{"deviceId":"extruder-1","protocol":"opcua","tagName":"Temperature","tagValue":20.645294745260895,"unit":"C","quality":"good","timestamp":"2026-09-27T20:21:58.255722Z"}]
```

This shape is the EmberNet dashboard's `TagValue` and is a contract. `quality`
is `good`, `uncertain` or `bad`; **a bad reading means the value is not known,
not that it is zero**. A string reading carries `stringVal`, and its
`tagValue` means nothing.

A reading that isn't good carries `reason` when the driver knows why, so a
screen can say more than "bad":

```json
{"deviceId":"meter-01","protocol":"http","tagName":"power","tagValue":0,"quality":"bad","timestamp":"2026-09-30T09:12:04.51Z","reason":"no field at ENERGY.Power"}
```

A good reading never has it, so the contract above is byte for byte what it
was. The historian doesn't keep it: `/api/history` has the quality, not the
reason.

### `GET /api/sparkline`

The last readings of one tag kept in memory (`HOTLOOP_RING_SIZE`, 30 by
default), for the little charts. `?tag=device/tag`, required.

```json
{"tag":"extruder-1/Temperature","timestamps":[1790540498609,1790540499246,1790540500246],"values":[0,20.06524581530632,19.933308705395785]}
```

`timestamps` are Unix milliseconds. Both are `[]` for a tag with no readings.
`400` for a malformed key.

### `GET /api/board`

Which tags are pinned to the board, and in how many columns. It is stored in
the database, not the browser, because a board belongs to the plant: the panel
PC on the floor and the laptop in the office show the same one.

```json
{"columns":2,"tags":["extruder-1/Temperature","tank-farm/level"]}
```

### `PUT /api/board`

The same shape. `columns` outside 1 to 4 becomes 3; duplicates are dropped.
Every tag must exist (`404` naming the one that does not): a stale entry is a
gauge that never moves. Answers the board as stored. Operators hold
`board.write`: arranging the board is running the plant, not configuring it.

### `POST /api/write`

Writes one value to one tag, through the write gate.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `tag` | string | Required. `device/tag` |
| `value` | bool, number or string | Required. `true` is a bool, `42` an integer, `42.5` a float, `"42"` a string: the JSON type is the type written, because a coil, a word and a real are three different things on the wire |
| `reason` | string | Optional. Logged with the write |

```json
{"tag":"tank-farm/level_sp","written":"72.5"}
```

The gate checks, in order, that writes are switched on
(`HOTLOOP_ALLOW_WRITES`), that the tag is armed, and that the value is in
range. Every attempt, refused or not, is in `GET /api/writes`.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | No value, a `null` value, a malformed key |
| 403 | Writes are off, or `"tank-farm/level: this tag is not marked writable"` |
| 404 | No such tag |
| 422 | `"value is outside the tag's configured range: 120 is outside 0..95"` |
| 503 | The device is not connected |

## History and audit

### `GET /api/history`

| Query | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| `tag` | Required, repeatable, up to 50: `?tag=a/x&tag=b/y` |
| `minutes` | How far back from now. Default 60 |
| `bucket` | Bucket size in seconds. Default: picked so the window is about 400 buckets, on a 1 s to 1 day ladder |
| `raw` | `true` for the readings themselves instead of buckets |
| `limit` | Default 5000, at most 100000 |
| `carry` | `true` to also say what each tag was holding when the window began (buckets only) |

Bucketed, oldest first per tag. `badCount` is how many readings in the bucket
were not good quality; they are counted, not averaged in. `from` and `to` are
the window the answer is for, exactly `minutes` apart and ending when the
question was asked:

```json
{"buckets":[{"deviceId":"extruder-1","tagName":"Temperature","bucket":"2026-09-27T20:21:00Z","avg":18.986210570239944,"min":0,"max":20.83008050535897,"first":0,"last":20.83008050535897,"count":22,"badCount":1}],"from":"2026-09-27T19:22:00Z","raw":false,"to":"2026-09-27T20:22:00Z"}
```

The historian keeps a reading when a value moves past its deadband, not on every
poll, so a tag that has held still has nothing in the window to draw. With
`carry=true` the answer also has `"carry":[{"deviceId":"extruder-1","tagName":"Temperature","ts":"2026-09-27T16:40:12Z","value":21.4}]`:
the last reading before `from`, for each tag whose last reading before it was
good and had a number in it. A tag whose last reading was bad or uncertain, that
has no earlier reading, or that is text, has no entry, because what it held isn't
known and I won't hand a chart a guess. The trend card draws from this.

Raw, newest first:

```json
{"raw":true,"readings":[{"deviceId":"extruder-1","protocol":"","tagName":"Temperature","tagValue":21.021559879601448,"quality":"good","timestamp":"2026-09-27T20:22:00.267463Z"}]}
```

`400` with no `tag`, more than 50, or a malformed key.

### `GET /api/writes`

The write audit, newest first. Every attempt is here, including the refused
ones, because "we do not know whether that command went out" is the worst
answer a plant can get.

| Query | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| `tag` | One tag, `device/tag` |
| `device` | Every tag on one device (ignored if `tag` is set) |
| `entity` | Every write a service call on this entity made or had refused, instead of the above |
| `call` | Every write of one call, instead of all of the above: a button's press and release, or every target of a recipe's application, which share its `call_id` |
| `limit` | Default 100, at most 5000 |

```json
[{"id":2,"at":"2026-09-27T20:22:01.04226Z","deviceId":"tank-farm","tagName":"level_sp","value":"120","prior":"0 %","actor":"admin","source":"ui","succeeded":false,"error":"refused: value is outside the tag's configured range: 120 is outside 0..95"},
 {"id":4,"at":"2026-09-27T20:23:03.276962Z","deviceId":"tank-farm","tagName":"pump","value":"true","prior":"0","actor":"admin","source":"ui","succeeded":true,"latencyMs":0.317,"entityId":"switch.tank_farm_pump","service":"switch.turn_on","callId":"5c9f8545a93b5443"}]
```

`source` is `ui`, `api`, `automation` or `mcp`. `entityId`, `service` and
`callId` are only on writes a service call made.

## Entities and states

Every tag gets entities without anybody asking; composites (motors, valves,
loops, counters, selects, buttons) are built from tags by an admin. Snake_case,
like every entity endpoint. The whole model is in [ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/).

### `GET /api/entities`

Every entity, orphans included.

| Query | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| `domain` | `sensor`, `switch`, `motor`... |
| `device` | Entities on one device |
| `orphaned` | `true` for only orphans, `false` for none |

```json
[{"id":5,"entity_id":"switch.tank_farm_pump","unique_id":"tag-control:tank-farm/pump","domain":"switch","platform":"tag","name":"pump","device_id":"tank-farm","options":{},"disabled":false,"hidden":false,"created_at":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.153197Z","updated_at":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.153197Z","bindings":[{"role":"command","device_id":"tank-farm","tag_name":"pump"},{"role":"state","device_id":"tank-farm","tag_name":"pump"}],"equipment_id":null,"area_id":4,"labels":[]}]
```

### `GET /api/entities/{entity_id}`

`{"entity": {...}, "state": {...}}`. `state` is `null` for a disabled entity.
`404` for an unknown one.

### `GET /api/entities/{entity_id}/image`

A camera's or an image's latest picture, as the bytes HotLoop holds:
`Content-Type` is what they are (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif` or
`image/webp`), with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a sandboxing
`Content-Security-Policy` and an `ETag` (`If-None-Match` gets a `304`). `404`
for an entity that isn't one, or before a picture has arrived. The state's
`entity_picture` attribute is this path with the picture's hash on it.

### `PUT /api/entities/{entity_id}`

Changes only the fields you send. Admin-only: the entity_id is the name every
automation, dashboard and agent refers to it by, and changing it is
configuration.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `entity_id` | string | A rename. The `unique_id` does not move |
| `name`, `icon`, `device_class`, `state_class`, `unit_of_measurement`, `entity_category` | string | |
| `options` | object | Per domain; see [ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/#api) |
| `disabled`, `hidden` | bool | A disabled entity has no state and cannot be commanded |
| `equipment_id` | int or null | Places it on the tree; `null` follows its device again |
| `labels` | string[] | The whole set |

`unique_id`, `domain`, `platform`, the device and the bindings cannot be
changed here, and sending them is a 400.

```json
{"entity":{"id":3,"entity_id":"sensor.tank_1_level","name":"Tank 1 level","device_class":"moisture","icon":"mdi:water-percent","...":"..."},"warnings":[]}
```

`warnings` says when something is legal but odd (a unit the device class does
not usually have). `400` for an empty body (`"the update names no field to
change"`) or a bad value, `404` for an unknown entity, `409` for an entity_id
that is taken.

### `POST /api/entities`

Creates a composite. The body names the domain and binds tags to its roles:

```json
{"name":"Transfer pump","domain":"motor","bindings":[{"role":"run_command","device_id":"tank-farm","tag_name":"pump"},{"role":"running","device_id":"tank-farm","tag_name":"pump"}]}
```

Also `entity_id` (else generated from the name), `device_class`,
`unit_of_measurement`, `icon`, `entity_category` and `options`. Which roles and
options each domain takes is in
[ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/#composite-equipment). Answers `201`
`{"entity": {...}, "warnings": [...]}`. `400` for a domain that is not
created here (a `sensor` comes from its tag, an `alarm` from its definition),
a missing role or a tag that cannot fill it, `409` for a taken entity_id.

### `DELETE /api/entities/{entity_id}`

Deletes a composite, or an orphan whose tag or alarm definition is gone.
`{"deleted":"motor.transfer_pump","entity":{...}}`. Anything else answers
`409` saying how it does go away:

```json
{"error":"this entity cannot be deleted: sensor.tank_1_level is kept in step with its tag; delete the tag, and then this orphan, or hide or disable it: already exists"}
```

### `GET /api/states`

Every enabled entity's state, ordered by entity_id. `?domain=` filters.

```json
[{"entity_id":"number.tank_farm_level_sp","state":"unknown","attributes":{"armed":true,"friendly_name":"level_sp","max":95,"min":0,"source":["tank-farm/level_sp"],"unit_of_measurement":"%"},"quality":"bad","last_changed":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.417193755Z","last_updated":"2026-09-27T20:21:39.417193755Z","last_reported":"2026-09-27T20:22:04.423849496Z"}]
```

`state` is always a string, even for a number; `unknown` and `unavailable`
mean what they say. `last_reported` is the device's timestamp of the reading
behind it.

### `GET /api/states/{entity_id}`

One state. `404` for an unknown entity, and a different `404` for a disabled
one, which says how to enable it: a disabled entity is not missing, and
reporting it as missing sends somebody hunting for a typo.

## Services

### `POST /api/services/{domain}/{service}`

Commands one entity: `switch/turn_on`, `number/set_value`, `motor/start`,
`alarm/acknowledge`. One entity, one service, one call. Underneath it is nothing but
tag writes through the same write gate as `POST /api/write`.

```json
{"entity_id":"switch.tank_farm_pump","reason":"start of shift"}
```

`entity_id` is required and is one entity, not a list; `reason` is optional;
everything else is the service's data (`value`, `option`, `position`, `mode`,
`minutes`, `note`). Numbers keep the type they were typed as. The domain in the
path must be the entity's. Every service and its data is in
[ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/#what-each-domain-takes).

```json
{"call_id":"5c9f8545a93b5443","entity_id":"switch.tank_farm_pump","service":"switch.turn_on","writes":[{"tag":"tank-farm/pump","value":"true","status":"written"}]}
```

Each write is `written`, `not_sent` (refused before it reached the device),
`failed` (it went out and the device reported an error, so whether it took is
not known) or `skipped` (an earlier write in the call did not succeed). Writes
already made are never rolled back. An alarm entity's services write no tag
and answer with the `alarm` as the engine left it. A helper's write no tag
either and answer with the `state` they left it in:

```json
{"call_id":"0f3c2a1b9d8e7f60","entity_id":"input_number.batch_target","service":"input_number.set_value","writes":[],"state":"1250"}
```

A script's `turn_on` runs it, with the data as its fields, and answers with the
`script_run` it started; its steps' writes are audited one by one as
`script:<id>`, not here. `turn_off` stops every run of it. See
[Scripts](#scripts).

A scene's `turn_on` applies its recipe, with `params` and `version` from the
data, and answers with the whole `recipe_application` and, in `writes`, every
write its targets made, in order. It fails unless every target was written.
See [Recipes](#recipes).

A failed call answers with the error's status and the same body plus `error`,
so you can see exactly where it stopped:

```json
{"error":"value is outside the tag's configured range: 150 is outside 0..95","call_id":"3cd42f8275e5765e","entity_id":"number.tank_farm_level_sp","service":"number.set_value","writes":[{"tag":"tank-farm/level_sp","value":"150","status":"not_sent","error":"value is outside the tag's configured range: 150 is outside 0..95"}]}
```

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | No `entity_id`, the wrong domain, an unknown service, data the service does not take |
| 403 | The permission, or the gate refused on policy |
| 404 | No such entity |
| 409 | A toggle with no known state, equipment in the wrong state for the service |
| 422 | A value refused on its merits |
| 503 | The device is not connected; the alarm engine is not running |
| 500 | A button press went out and its release did not. **The tag may still hold the press value**: check it and release it by hand |

**`?dry_run=true`** asks what the call would do and does none of it: nothing is
written, audited or logged. The call is planned as the real one is and every
write is put to the gate's own checks, in the same order, right now. A verdict
answers 200, refused or not: each write `would_write`, or the first that would
be refused `not_sent` with the reason and the rest `skipped`, and `error` is
the error the real call would fail with, word for word.

```json
{"dry_run":true,"error":"value is outside the tag's configured range: 150 is outside 0..95","entity_id":"number.tank_farm_level_sp","service":"number.set_value","writes":[{"tag":"tank-farm/level_sp","value":"150","status":"not_sent","error":"value is outside the tag's configured range: 150 is outside 0..95"}]}
```

A request the real call would turn away before any check (no such entity, an
unknown service, data the service does not take, a toggle with no known state)
answers with the real call's status and error; so does a missing permission.
`dry_run` is `true` or `false` and nothing else: `yes` is a 400, not a guess,
because guessing wrong turns a question into a command. See
[ENTITIES.md](/iot/entities/#asking-first-the-dry-run).

**Why the permission is checked in the handler.** It needs `values.write`, the
same as writing the tag directly, because that is all it is; an `alarm`
entity's services need `alarms.ack` instead, the same as the alarm screen, a
helper's need `helpers.write`, which an operator holds, and a script's need
`scripts.run`, the same as `POST /api/scripts/{id}/run`, and a scene's need
`recipes.apply` and the recipe's own permission when it names one, the same as
`POST /api/recipes/{id}/apply`. The
check is made inside the handler rather than in front of it so that a refusal
for want of it is sent to the write gate and **audited against the entity**
like every other refusal, with the value that was asked for. A user without the
permission gets a 403 and a line in `GET /api/writes?entity=...`, not a 403 and
nothing. A helper writes no tag, so a helper's refusal, this one included, is a
warning in the system log (`GET /api/events`) against the helper instead, and
so is a script's. A scene's refusal is a refused application in the recipe's
history, with the user on it.

## Helpers

Values the plant's people own rather than a PLC: `input_boolean`,
`input_number`, `input_select`, `input_text`, `input_counter`, `timer` and
`schedule`. A helper is an entity (platform `helper`) and shows up in
`/api/entities` and `/api/states` like any other; these routes are its
configuration. Its value is set through its services above, with
`helpers.write`. Every domain, option and service is in
[HELPERS.md](/iot/helpers/).

### `GET /api/helpers`

Every helper, each with its entity's fields and `value`, the row stored for it:

```json
[{"id":41,"entity_id":"timer.purge","unique_id":"helper:6f1d...","domain":"timer","platform":"helper","name":"Purge","options":{"duration_sec":600},"...":"...","value":{"state":"active","finishes_at":"2026-09-27T21:10:00Z","duration_ms":600000,"changed_at":"2026-09-27T21:00:00Z","changed_by":"otto","source":"ui","call_id":"9a1b...","rev":4}}]
```

### `POST /api/helpers`

Creates a helper at its initial value. Admin-only.

```json
{"name":"Batch target","domain":"input_number","unit_of_measurement":"kg","options":{"min":0,"max":5000,"step":50,"initial":1000}}
```

Also `entity_id` (else generated from the name) and `icon`. Answers `201`
`{"helper": {...}}`. `400` for a domain that is not a helper's, an option the
domain does not take, or an `initial` its own options would refuse; `409` for
a taken entity_id.

### `GET /api/helpers/{entity_id}`

One helper, as in the list. `404` for an unknown entity or one that is not a
helper.

### `PUT /api/helpers/{entity_id}`

Changes its `name`, `icon`, `unit_of_measurement`, `options`, `disabled`,
`hidden`, `entity_id`, `equipment_id` or `labels`, the same fields as
`PUT /api/entities/{entity_id}`. Admin-only. New options that would not allow
the value it holds now (a range narrowed past it, the selected choice
removed) are a `400`: a value is never moved to fit. Answers
`{"helper": {...}, "warnings": []}`.

### `DELETE /api/helpers/{entity_id}`

Deletes the helper and its value. Admin-only. `{"deleted":"timer.purge"}`.
`DELETE /api/entities/{entity_id}` refuses a helper with a `409` pointing
here.

## Equipment and labels

The ISA-95 tree (enterprise, site, area, line, cell, unit, equipment) and
free-form labels. Snake_case. Every role reads; only an admin changes, because
renaming or moving a node rewrites the site, area and line of every device
under it. See [EQUIPMENT.md](/iot/equipment/).

### `GET /api/equipment`

Every node, ordered by id, each with its `path` of names from the root.
`?level=area` filters.

```json
[{"id":4,"parent_id":1,"level":"area","name":"Utilities","created_at":"2026-09-27T20:21:01.637319Z","updated_at":"2026-09-27T20:21:01.637319Z","path":["Demo Plant","Utilities"]}]
```

### `POST /api/equipment`

```json
{"parent_id":3,"level":"cell","name":"Die head","description":"Die and screen changer"}
```

`parent_id` null or left out makes a root. A child must be a lower level than
its parent (equipment may sit in equipment). Answers
`{"equipment": {...}, "devices_rewritten": []}`. `400` for a bad level or
placement, `409` for a sibling with the same level and name.

### `GET /api/equipment/{id}`

The node, the nodes directly under it, and the devices and entities placed
directly on it:

```json
{"children":[],"devices":["extruder-1"],"entities":[],"equipment":{"id":3,"parent_id":2,"level":"line","name":"Line 1","...":"...","path":["Demo Plant","Extrusion","Line 1"]}}
```
