`400` for an id that is not a positive number, `404` for an unknown one.

### `PUT /api/equipment/{id}`

Any of `name`, `description`, `level`, `parent_id` (`null` moves it to the
root). Only the fields sent change; an empty body is a 400. Answers the node and
**every device whose site, area or line text changed as a result**, because
that text is what older clients and the MCP tools read:

```json
{"devices_rewritten":["tank-farm"],"equipment":{"id":4,"parent_id":1,"level":"area","name":"Utilities East","...":"..."}}
```

### `DELETE /api/equipment/{id}`

`{"deleted":5}`. `409` while anything is under it or placed on it, saying what:
deleting a node out from under a device is not a decision to make by
accident.

### `GET /api/labels`

```json
[{"label_id":"critical","name":"Critical","color":"red","icon":"mdi:alert","description":"Stops the line if it fails","created_at":"2026-09-27T20:24:29.659126Z","updated_at":"2026-09-27T20:24:29.659126Z"}]
```

### `POST /api/labels`

`name` is required; `label_id` (1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, underscores)
is generated from the name if left out, and never changes afterwards. `color`,
`icon` (`mdi:...`) and `description` are optional. Answers the label. `409` for
a name or id that is taken.

### `GET /api/labels/{label_id}`

`{"label": {...}, "devices": ["tank-farm"], "entities": []}`: the label and what
carries it. `404` for an unknown one.

### `PUT /api/labels/{label_id}`

Replaces `name`, `color`, `icon` and `description`; a field left out is
cleared. A `label_id` in the body must match the path: `400` otherwise, because
a label_id never changes.

### `DELETE /api/labels/{label_id}`

Removes it from everything carrying it. `{"deleted":"critical"}`, or `404`.

### `PUT /api/devices/{id}/labels`

`{"labels": ["critical"]}` replaces the whole set on a device. Answers
`{"id":"tank-farm","labels":["critical"]}`. Every label must exist (`400`
naming the missing ones), and the device too (`404`). Labels are not part of
`POST /api/devices` on purpose: every client that saves a device sends the
whole device without them, and would wipe them on every save.

## Alarms

ISA-18.2: raising, acknowledging and returning to normal are separate things,
and the log can tell which happened.

### `GET /api/alarms`

Every definition, the live alarms and the summary. `?outstanding=true` leaves
out the normal and silenced ones.

```json
{
  "alarms": [{"definitionId":"extruder-temp-hi","name":"Extruder temperature high","deviceId":"extruder-1","tagName":"Temperature","priority":2,"state":"unack-active","message":"extruder-1/Temperature at 22.80197037650447 C, limit 5","tripValue":22.80197037650447,"raisedAt":"2026-09-27T20:25:19.67042816Z","count":1,"updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:25:19.67042816Z"}],
  "definitions": [{"id":"extruder-temp-hi","name":"Extruder temperature high","deviceId":"extruder-1","tagName":"Temperature","condition":"hi","limit":5,"priority":2,"enabled":true,"deadband":0.5,"message":"{device}/{tag} at {value}, limit {limit}","createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:25:19.055658Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:25:19.055658Z"}],
  "summary": {"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0,"unacked":1,"total":1}
}
```

`state` is `normal`, `unack-active`, `ack-active`, `rtn-unack` (cleared before
anyone acknowledged it, and kept on the list so a 3am trip cannot vanish before
the morning shift sees it), `shelved` or `suppressed`. `tripValue` is the
reading that raised it, not the current one.

### `POST /api/alarms`

Creates or replaces a definition.

| Field | Type | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `id`, `name` | string | Required. `id` follows the device id rules |
| `deviceId`, `tagName` | string | Required |
| `condition` | string | `hihi`, `hi`, `lo`, `lolo`, `eq`, `ne`, `true`, `false`, `bad-quality`, `stale` (no reading for `limit` seconds), `roc` (rate of change above `limit` per second) |
| `limit` | number | |
| `priority` | int | 1 (critical) to 4 (low) |
| `enabled` | bool | Left out is `false` |
| `deadband` | number | How far back the value must come before it clears. Without one, a value sitting on the limit chatters |
| `onDelaySec`, `offDelaySec` | int | How long the condition must hold before it raises, or be clear before it returns to normal |
| `message`, `description` | string | `message` takes `{value}`, `{limit}`, `{tag}`, `{device}`, `{unit}`, `{condition}` and `{reason}` (why the reading is bad, empty when it is good) |

`{value}` is written the way the value card writes it, unit included: whole
numbers as they are, two places from 1 up, one from 100 up, four below 1, and
scientific past ten million or under 0.01 (`8.20 pH`, `212.5 F`, `1.235e+7`).
I did that because a tag with scale 0.1 and a raw 82 is 8.200000000000001 as a
float, and the banner used to say so. A text reading is said as it is. The tag
itself, the writes and the automations still see the exact number; only the
sentence is rounded. `{limit}` is the limit as you typed it.

Answers the definition; the engine reloads and the alarm entity is made before
the answer. `400` on a failed validation (`"alarm x: priority must be 1-4, got
9"`).

### `DELETE /api/alarms/{id}`

`{"deleted":"extruder-temp-hi"}`, or `404`.

### `POST /api/alarms/{id}/ack`

Optional body `{"note": "checking the heater bands"}`. Answers the alarm as it
now is, with `ackedBy` and `ackNote`. `404` for an unknown alarm.

### `POST /api/alarms/{id}/shelve`

`{"minutes": 30}`, required and positive: an indefinite silence is a
suppression, which is a different thing and not an operator's to make. Answers
the alarm, `state` `shelved`, with `shelvedUntil` and `shelvedBy`.

### `POST /api/alarms/{id}/unshelve`

No body. Answers the alarm back in whatever state its condition puts it. `409`
if it was not shelved.

### `GET /api/alarms/events`

The alarm audit trail, newest first. `?alarm=` one definition, `?limit=`
(default 200, at most 5000).

```json
[{"id":2,"definitionId":"extruder-temp-hi","type":"acked","fromState":"unack-active","toState":"ack-active","value":23.192472931395088,"message":"extruder-1/Temperature at 22.80197037650447 C, limit 5","actor":"admin","note":"checking the heater bands","at":"2026-09-27T20:25:22.920251Z"}]
```

`type` is `raised`, `acked`, `cleared`, `shelved`, `unshelved`, `suppressed`,
`unsuppressed`, `escalated` or `escalation-ended`. The last two are written by
alarm escalation (`actor` is `escalation`), and their `note` says who was told
and why the chain stopped. See [NOTIFY.md](/iot/notifications/#escalation).

## Automations

Triggers, a condition, actions. The rule language is in
[AUTOMATIONS.md](/iot/automations/).

### `GET /api/automations`

```json
{"armed":{"fill-tank":true},"automations":[{"id":"fill-tank","name":"Fill the tank","enabled":true,"triggers":[{"type":"threshold","deviceId":"tank-farm","tagName":"level","threshold":20,"direction":"falling","hysteresis":5},{"type":"webhook","webhookPath":"fill-now"}],"actions":[{"type":"call_service","name":"start the pump","params":{"service":"switch.turn_on","entityId":"switch.tank_farm_pump"}}],"mode":"skip","minIntervalSec":60,"createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:26:49.770826Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:26:49.770826Z"}],"webhooks":["fill-now"]}
```

`armed` is which rules are actually running, which is not the same as
`enabled`: an enabled rule that stopped compiling is not armed, and this is
where you find out.

### `POST /api/automations`

Creates or replaces a rule: `id`, `name`, `description`, `enabled`,
`triggers` (at least one), `condition`, `actions` (at least one), `mode`
(`skip`, the default, `queue`, `restart` or `parallel`), `minIntervalSec`,
`maxRuntimeSec`. The rule is compiled before it is stored, and one that does not
compile is a 400 and never reaches the database: a stored rule that cannot be
armed is a rule its author believes is running.

```json
{"error":"automation fill-tank action 1 (call_service): params: json: unknown field \"entity_id\""}
```

### `POST /api/automations/validate`

Compiles a rule without saving it, for the editor's live check. Always `200`;
the answer says whether it compiled:

```json
{"valid":true}
{"error":"automation bad: at least one trigger is required","valid":false}
```

It needs `automations.write` because it exists to help somebody write one.

### `DELETE /api/automations/{id}`

`{"deleted":"fill-tank"}`, or `404`.

### `POST /api/automations/{id}/enabled`

`{"enabled": false}` disarms it without deleting it. Answers
`{"enabled":false,"id":"fill-tank"}`, or `404`.

### `POST /api/automations/{id}/trigger`

Runs it now, as if a trigger fired. The condition still applies (a false one
records a `skipped` run) and so does the run mode; `minIntervalSec` does not,
because a person asking for a run is not a chattering tag. No body. `202` `{"triggered":"fill-tank"}`: the run happens in the
background, and `GET /api/runs` has the result. `400` if the rule is not armed.
Operators hold `automations.trigger`; running a rule somebody else wrote is
operating, writing one is not.

### `GET /api/runs`

Run history, newest first. `?automation=` one rule, `?limit=` (default 100, at
most 1000). `[]` when there are none.

```json
[{"id":1,"automationId":"fill-tank","status":"succeeded","triggerType":"manual","triggerDesc":"triggered by admin","actor":"admin","startedAt":"2026-09-27T20:26:50.269792Z","finishedAt":"2026-09-27T20:26:50.282129Z","durationMs":12.337,"steps":[{"index":1,"type":"call_service","name":"start the pump","input":"switch.turn_on switch.tank_farm_pump {}","output":"true to tank-farm/pump: written; call 8fb9538c82d532be","startedAt":"2026-09-27T20:26:50.272532641Z","durationMs":9.595}]}]
```

`status` is `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `skipped`, `timed_out` or
`cancelled`. The steps keep the resolved inputs, not the templates, because
that is what you need to read at 3am.

A rule made from a blueprint carries three more fields in `GET
/api/automations`: `blueprintId`, `blueprintVersion` (the version it was made
from, which is the version it stays at) and `blueprintInputs`. A rule written
by hand has none of them. They are the server's: `POST /api/automations`
accepts them and ignores them, and an edit by hand keeps whatever the rule had.

### `POST /api/automations/{id}/blueprint-upgrade`

Moves a rule made from a blueprint to the blueprint's newest version, keeping
its id, its name and whether it is armed. It is never done for you. Operators
hold `blueprints.apply`, the same as for making one. Look first:
**`?dry_run=true`** changes nothing and answers what would change, part by
part, and what the rule would then do if it fired now, every write put to the
gate's checks:

```json
{"dry_run":true,"id":"pump_1_watch","blueprint":"pump_watch","from":1,"to":2,"changes":[{"field":"actions","before":[{"params":{"message":"switch.pump_1 started, v1"},"type":"log_event"}],"after":[{"params":{"message":"switch.pump_1 started, v2"},"type":"log_event"}]}],"automation":{"id":"pump_1_watch","...":"..."},"check":{"automation_id":"pump_1_watch","steps":[{"step":"1","type":"log_event","verdict":"not_checked","detail":"a dry run checks writes to equipment; this step writes to none and runs only for real"}]}}
```

An edit made by hand since the rule was made shows up in `changes` as being
replaced. When the new version needs an input the rule has no value for, or
refuses a value it was made with, the dry run says so in `error` and nothing
else.

The real one takes `{"version": 2}`, the version the dry run showed, and
`inputs` for anything the new version needs. A blueprint that moved on since,
or a rule somebody upgraded in the meantime, is a `409`: what was reviewed is
what goes in, or nothing does. A missing input is a `400`. `200` with the
same shape, `automation` being the rule as stored. It is logged as
`automation upgraded from blueprint pump_watch version 1 to 2`. With the same
version and new `inputs`, it is how a rule's inputs are changed. `400` for a
rule written by hand; `404` if the blueprint it came from is gone.

## Scripts

Named sequences of actions, run on demand: from here, from a rule's
`call_script` step, from MCP's `run_script`, or through the script's entity
(`script.turn_on`). The sequence is the automation language. Every write a
step makes goes through the write gate as `script:<id>`, with the source of
whoever started it. Everything is in [SCRIPTS.md](/iot/scripts/).

### `GET /api/scripts`

Every script, with its run counters and how many runs of it are going now,
in any process:

```json
[{"id":"cip_cycle","name":"CIP cycle","fields":[{"name":"minutes","type":"number","required":true,"min":1,"max":60,"unit":"min"}],"sequence":[{"type":"call_service","params":{"entityId":"switch.cip_pump","service":"switch.turn_on"}}],"mode":"skip","createdAt":"2026-09-28T10:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-28T10:00:00Z","lastRun":"2026-09-28T10:05:00Z","lastStatus":"succeeded","runCount":3,"running":0}]
```

### `POST /api/scripts`

Creates one. Admin-only. `id` (lowercase letters, digits and underscores,
starting with a letter: it is the entity's object id, `script.<id>`), `name`,
`description`, `icon`, `fields` (typed inputs), `sequence` (at least one
action), `mode` (`skip`, the default, `queue`, `restart` or `parallel`) and
`maxRuntimeSec`. It is compiled before it is stored, like a rule, and a script
that would call itself, directly or through other scripts, is refused. Answers
`201` with the script. `400` for anything that does not compile; `409` for an id
that is taken.

### `POST /api/scripts/validate`

Checks a script without saving it, for the editor's live check. `200`
`{"valid":true}` or `{"valid":false,"error":"..."}`, in the words a save would
be refused with.

### `GET /api/scripts/{id}`

One script, as in the list. `404` if there is none.

### `PUT /api/scripts/{id}`

Replaces its definition; the body is the same as for creating one, and its `id`
may be left out. Admin-only. Runs of it in progress are cancelled when its
steps, fields or mode change: they were started from the old definition.

### `DELETE /api/scripts/{id}`

Deletes it and its run history, cancelling its runs in progress. Admin-only.
`{"deleted":"cip_cycle"}`. Its entity is orphaned, not deleted.

### `POST /api/scripts/{id}/run`

Runs it. Operators hold `scripts.run`.

```json
{"fields":{"minutes":20},"reason":"end of shift clean","wait":false}
```

Every field is optional in the body, and so is the body. The fields are checked
against the script's before anything runs: a value out of range, off its step,
not one of the options or of the wrong type is a `400`, and is never moved to
fit. `202` with the run as soon as it has started; with `"wait":true`, `200`
with the run once it has ended, its trace included.

```json
{"run":{"id":77,"scriptId":"cip_cycle","status":"running","actor":"otto","source":"ui","fields":{"minutes":20},"startedAt":"2026-09-28T10:05:00Z","durationMs":0}}
```

`409` when it is busy: running already and its mode is `skip`, or running with
one queued and its mode is `queue`. Nothing ran, and a `skipped` run is in the
history saying why:

```json
{"error":"script busy: script cip_cycle was not started: it is already running, and its mode is skip","run":{"id":78,"scriptId":"cip_cycle","status":"skipped","...":"..."}}
```

**`?dry_run=true`** asks what a run would do now and does none of it. The fields
are checked the same way; then each step is walked against the plant as it
is: every write and service call is put to the gate's own checks, a condition
is evaluated, a variable bound. A wait, a delay and anything that writes to
no equipment are `not_checked`. The first write that would be refused ends
it, as it would end the run, and `error` says so in the gate's words. `200`
with the verdict, refused or not:

```json
{"dry_run":true,"check":{"script_id":"cip_cycle","fields":{"minutes":20},"steps":[{"step":"1","type":"call_service","input":"switch.turn_on switch.cip_pump {}","verdict":"refused","detail":"cip/pump: this tag is not marked writable"}],"error":"step 1 (call_service): cip/pump: this tag is not marked writable"}}
```

Each step's `verdict` is `would_write`, `refused`, `ends_here` (a condition
false now, or a stop), `not_checked` or `ok`. A step of a script it calls is
numbered under the call: `3.1`.

### `POST /api/scripts/{id}/stop`

Cancels every run of it in progress, in every process, where it is.
`{"cancelled":1,"stopped":"cip_cycle"}`, `cancelled` being the runs this process
had. Operators hold `scripts.run`: stopping what you may start is part of
starting it.

### `GET /api/scripts/{id}/runs`

Its runs, newest first, with their traces. `?limit=` (default 50, at most
1000). `parent` is what called a run, when something did:
`automation_run:812`, `script_run:77`.

```json
[{"id":77,"scriptId":"cip_cycle","status":"succeeded","actor":"automation:shift-end","source":"automation","parent":"automation_run:812","fields":{"minutes":20},"startedAt":"2026-09-28T10:05:00Z","finishedAt":"2026-09-28T10:25:00Z","durationMs":1200012,"steps":[{"index":1,"type":"call_service","input":"switch.turn_on switch.cip_pump {}","output":"true to cip/pump: written; call 8fb9538c82d532be","startedAt":"2026-09-28T10:05:00Z","durationMs":9.6}]}]
```

## Recipes

Sets of values applied together: a product grade's setpoints, a changeover.
Each one is also an entity, `scene.<id>`.
A recipe is checked whole before anything goes out and refused whole on any
reason; its targets then go out in order under one call id, the first that
fails stops the rest, and nothing is undone; every written value is read back
from the device. Everything is in [RECIPES.md](/iot/recipes/).

A recipe's name, description, equipment node and permission change in place.
What it writes (`targets`, `params`, `precondition`, `verify_sec`) is a
version, and versions are never changed: saving new content stores the next
one.

### `GET /api/recipes`

Every recipe, with its current version's content and its newest application:

```json
[{"id":"grade_a","name":"Grade A","equipment_id":7,"apply_permission":"recipes.apply","current_version":3,"params":[{"name":"speed","type":"number","min":0,"max":400,"step":10,"unit":"rpm","required":true}],"precondition":"states['input_boolean.line_ready'] == 'on'","targets":[{"entity_id":"number.line_02_zone1_sp","service":"set_value","data":{"value":210}},{"entity_id":"number.line_02_speed","service":"set_value","data_expressions":{"value":"vars.speed"}}],"verify_sec":10,"note":"zone 1 up 5","created_at":"2026-09-28T10:00:00Z","updated_at":"2026-09-28T11:00:00Z","last_application":{"id":41,"recipe_id":"grade_a","version":3,"call_id":"7c1f0e2d9a8b6c54","actor":"otto","source":"ui","params":{"speed":250},"status":"applied","targets":[],"started_at":"2026-09-28T11:05:00Z","finished_at":"2026-09-28T11:05:01Z"}}]
```

`equipment_id` is `null` for a recipe of the whole plant.

### `POST /api/recipes`

Creates one, as version 1. Admin-only. `id` (lowercase letters, digits and
underscores, starting with a letter: it is the entity's object id,
`scene.<id>`), `name`, `description`, `equipment_id`, `apply_permission`
(`recipes.apply`, the default, or `recipes.apply.<name>`), `params` (typed
inputs), `precondition` (an expression that must be true to start),
`targets` (at least one, at most 200, each `entity_id`, `service` and `data`
or `data_expressions`), `verify_sec` (1 to 600, default 10) and `note`. A
target sets a value: `set_value`, `select_option`, `set_position`,
`set_speed`, `set_setpoint`, `set_mode`, `turn_on`, `turn_off`, on the domains
that take them. A pulse or a start is refused: it belongs in a script. Every
target's entity must exist, and every expression must compile. `201` with the
recipe; `400` for anything wrong, `409` for an id that is taken.

### `POST /api/recipes/capture`

Drafts a recipe from what entities hold now, admin-only, and saves nothing:

```json
{"entity_ids":["number.line_02_zone1_sp","switch.line_02_heater","loop.line_02_tic"]}
```

Each becomes a target that sets it back to its current value, in the order
given; a loop becomes its mode and then its setpoint. The answer is a recipe
without an id or a name, for the editor. An entity that does not exist, is
disabled, reads with a quality other than good, is `unknown` or
`unavailable`, or is not something a recipe sets is a `400` naming every one
of them: a recipe built from a bad reading writes the bad reading back.

### `GET /api/recipes/{id}`

One recipe, as in the list. `404` if there is none.

### `PUT /api/recipes/{id}`

Saves it. Admin-only. The body is the recipe as `GET` answered it, edited; its
`id` may be left out. `current_version` is the version the edit was made to:
if somebody has saved another since, the save is a `409` rather than a quiet
overwrite of theirs (`0` skips the check). New content becomes the next
version, with `note` saying why; a change to only the name, description,
equipment or permission makes none.

### `DELETE /api/recipes/{id}`

Deletes it and its versions. Admin-only. `{"deleted":"grade_a"}`. Its
applications are kept, because they are what was sent to the plant, and its
entity is orphaned.

### `GET /api/recipes/{id}/versions`

Every version, newest first, each exactly as it was saved, with who saved it
and the note:

```json
[{"recipe_id":"grade_a","version":3,"params":[],"targets":[{"entity_id":"number.line_02_zone1_sp","service":"set_value","data":{"value":210}}],"verify_sec":10,"note":"zone 1 up 5","created_by":"ada","created_at":"2026-09-28T11:00:00Z"}]
```

### `GET /api/recipes/{id}/versions/{version}`

One version. `404` if the recipe has no such version, `400` if `{version}` is
not a number.

### `POST /api/recipes/{id}/validate`

Would it apply right now? Operators hold `recipes.apply`. The body is an
apply's, and nothing is written, recorded or logged. Every check an
application makes before it writes is made: the parameters, the recipe's own
permission, the precondition, the data expressions, whether another
application is writing to one of its entities, and every target put to the
write gate's checks. `200` with the verdict, `would_apply` or `refused`, and
every target's own: `would_write`, `refused` with the reason, or `not_sent`.

```json
{"dry_run":true,"application":{"recipe_id":"grade_a","version":3,"params":{"speed":250},"status":"refused","targets":[{"index":1,"entity_id":"number.line_02_zone1_sp","service":"set_value","data":{"value":210},"status":"would_write"},{"index":2,"entity_id":"number.line_02_speed","service":"set_value","data":{"value":250},"status":"refused","error":"line-02/Speed: this tag is not marked writable"}],"started_at":"2026-09-28T11:04:00Z","error":"target 2 (set_value number.line_02_speed): line-02/Speed: this tag is not marked writable"}}
```

Parameters it does not take are a `400`, as they would be for the real thing.

### `POST /api/recipes/{id}/apply`

Applies it. Operators hold `recipes.apply`. A recipe that names a permission
of its own, `recipes.apply.<name>`, takes that as well, checked here against
the recipe; a user without it gets a `403` and a refused application in the
history with their name on it.

```json
{"params":{"speed":250},"reason":"grade A for the 2pm run","version":0,"resume":0}
```

Everything is optional, and so is the body. `version` applies an older
version on purpose; left out, the current one. `resume` is the id of an
earlier application of this recipe that stopped halfway: its targets that
were not written go out as a new application, with its version and
parameters, and `parent` says which it finishes.

It answers once every value has been written and read back, which takes up to
the recipe's `verify_sec`:

```json
{"application":{"id":42,"recipe_id":"grade_a","version":3,"call_id":"9d2e4f6a8b0c1e3f","actor":"otto","source":"ui","reason":"grade A for the 2pm run","params":{"speed":250},"status":"applied","targets":[{"index":1,"entity_id":"number.line_02_zone1_sp","service":"set_value","data":{"value":210},"status":"written","writes":[{"tag":"line-02/Zone1_SP","value":"210","status":"written"}],"verification":"verified","verify_detail":"read back 210"},{"index":2,"entity_id":"number.line_02_speed","service":"set_value","data":{"value":250},"status":"written","writes":[{"tag":"line-02/Speed","value":"250","status":"written"}],"verification":"unconfirmed","verify_detail":"not confirmed within 10s: read back 240, not 250"}],"started_at":"2026-09-28T11:05:00Z","finished_at":"2026-09-28T11:05:10Z"}}
```

A target is `written`, `failed` (it went out and the device said no, or said
nothing), `not_sent`, `skipped` (one before it did not go through) or
`refused` (pre-validation). A written one is `verified` when the device read
back the value it was sent after it was sent, and `unconfirmed` when it did
not within `verify_sec`: it went out and it may not have taken. Every write
carries the application's `call_id`, so `GET /api/writes?call=<call_id>` is
all of them.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 200 | `applied`: every target written. Check each one's `verification` |
| 400 | A parameter the recipe does not take, out of range or of the wrong type; a `resume` of nothing left to apply |
| 403 | The recipe's own permission. Recorded as a refused application |
| 404 | No such recipe, or no such version |
| 409 | `refused`: any reason not to start, every one in `error` and on its target. Or another application is writing to one of its entities right now. Nothing was written |
| 502 | `partial` or `failed`: it started, and not every target went out. `targets` says exactly which did. Nothing is undone |

Every answer but a `400` for a malformed body or a `404` carries the
application, and every application but a dry run is in
`GET /api/recipes/{id}/applications`, refusals included.

### `GET /api/recipes/{id}/applications`

Its applications, newest first, refused ones included. `?limit=` (default 50,
at most 1000). `parent` is what applied it, when something did:
`automation_run:812`, `script_run:77`, `application:41`. A deleted recipe's
applications are still answered.

## Blueprints

An automation written once with typed blanks in it, filled in to make an
ordinary rule. The rule keeps the version it was made from; editing the
blueprint changes no rule, and moving one to a newer version is
[an upgrade](#post-apiautomationsidblueprint-upgrade) somebody asks for. Every
write the rule makes goes through the write gate as `automation:<id>`.
Everything is in [BLUEPRINTS.md](/iot/blueprints/).

### `GET /api/blueprints`

Every blueprint, the built-in ones first, each with how many rules were made
from it:

```json
[{"id":"motor_running_too_long","name":"Motor running too long","description":"Says so when a motor has been running longer than it should...","source":"builtin","version":1,"inputs":[{"name":"motor","label":"Motor","type":"entity","required":true,"domain":["motor"]},{"name":"max_run","label":"Longest it may run","type":"duration","default":3600},{"name":"stop_it","label":"Stop it as well","type":"boolean","default":false}],"template":{"triggers":[{"type":"state","entityId":{"!input":"motor"},"to":"running","forSec":{"!input":"max_run"}}],"...":"..."},"instances":2}]
```

`source` is `builtin` (ships in the binary, read-only) or `user`.

### `POST /api/blueprints`

Writes one. Admin-only. `id` (lowercase letters, digits and underscores,
starting with a letter), `name`, `description`, `inputs` (typed, the same as a
script's fields) and `template`: the rule, with its `description`,
`triggers`, `condition`, `actions`, `mode`, `minIntervalSec` and
`maxRuntimeSec`, and the blanks in it. `{"!input": "motor"}` as a value is
replaced by the input; `${motor}` in a string is too, as a literal where the
string is an expression. It is checked before it is stored: every blank names
an input, every input is used, and filled in with sample values it makes a
rule that compiles. `201` at `version` 1. `400` for anything wrong with it,
`409` for an id that is taken, a built-in one's included.

### `GET /api/blueprints/{id}`

One, as in the list. `404` if there is none.

### `PUT /api/blueprints/{id}`

Replaces its definition; the body is the same as for writing one, and its `id`
may be left out. Admin-only. `version` goes up by one when `inputs` or
`template` changed, and not for a new name or description. **No rule made from
it changes.** Each keeps the version it was made from, and
`GET /api/automations` shows which. A built-in one is a `400`: copy it under an
id of your own.

### `DELETE /api/blueprints/{id}`

Admin-only. `{"deleted":"pump_watch"}`. `409` while any rule made from it
exists, naming them: delete those first. A built-in one is a `400`.

### `POST /api/blueprints/{id}/instantiate`

Makes a rule from it and arms it. Operators hold `blueprints.apply`: which
pump and how long is theirs to pick, and what the rule does was decided when
the blueprint was written.

```json
{"automationId":"infeed_too_long","name":"Infeed pump ran too long","enabled":true,"inputs":{"motor":"motor.infeed_pump","max_run":"90m","stop_it":true}}
```

`name` defaults to the blueprint's and `enabled` to `true`. Every input is
checked before anything is made: a value out of range, off its step, not one
of its options, an entity of another domain, or of the wrong type is a `400`
naming every one that is wrong, and is never moved to fit. An `automationId`
that is taken is a `409`: making a rule never replaces one. `201` with the
rule, its `blueprintId`, `blueprintVersion` and `blueprintInputs` set. It is
logged as `automation made from blueprint motor_running_too_long version 1`.

**`?dry_run=true`** makes nothing. It answers the rule it would make and what
that rule would do if it fired now: the condition evaluated, every write and
service call put to the gate's checks as `automation:<id>`, the first refusal
in `check.error` in the gate's words. Nothing is stored, written or audited.

```json
{"dry_run":true,"automation":{"id":"infeed_too_long","...":"..."},"check":{"automation_id":"infeed_too_long","steps":[{"step":"1","type":"log_event","verdict":"not_checked"},{"step":"2","type":"condition","input":"true","verdict":"ok","detail":"true now"},{"step":"3","type":"call_service","input":"motor.stop motor.infeed_pump {}","verdict":"would_write","detail":"would write false to line-02/M1_Run"}]}}
```

## Dashboards

Pages of cards, for the roles and the screens that need them. A dashboard
commands nothing: a card names a tag, an entity, a script or a recipe, and its
button writes through [`POST /api/write`](#post-apiwrite) as the person who
pressed it. The wall board is one of them. Everything is in
[DASHBOARDS.md](/iot/dashboards/).

### `GET /api/dashboards`

The dashboards the caller is offered, in the order the switcher shows them,
the wall board included. Whoever holds `dashboards.write` is offered all of
them.

```json
[{"id":"wall","name":"Wall board","description":"The tags pinned on the Board screen, as gauges.","kind":"wall","roles":[],"homeFor":[],"screens":["wall-tv"],"position":0,"cards":[],"version":2,"updatedBy":"ada"},
 {"id":"line-2","name":"Line 2","kind":"cards","roles":["operator","admin"],"homeFor":["operator"],"screens":["line-2-panel"],"position":1,"version":3,"updatedBy":"ada","cards":[{"id":"temp","type":"gauge","title":"Zone 1","w":3,"h":3,"config":{"tag":"press-01/Zone1_Temp"}}]}]
```

### `POST /api/dashboards`

Builds one. Admin-only. `id` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and
underscores, starting with a letter), `name`, and optionally `description`,
`roles`, `homeFor`, `screens`, `position` and `cards`. `201` at `version` 1,
with every card's size and config in the form that was stored.

A card is `id`, `type`, `title`, `w` (1 to 12 columns), `h` (1 to 8 rows) and a
`config`. The types and their configs are in
[DASHBOARDS.md](/iot/dashboards/#the-cards). It is checked before it is stored:

- a config key the type does not have, a number out of range, a camera or
  floor-plan address with a login or token in it, or more than 60 cards is a
  `400`;
- a card that names a tag, entity, script or recipe that does not exist is a
  `400` naming it;
- a `button` on a tag that is not writable, or with a number outside the tag's
  range, is a `400`: the gate would refuse every press;
- a role that does not exist is a `400`;
- an `id` that is taken, a screen another dashboard already has, or a role's
  home another dashboard already is, is a `409`.

### `GET /api/dashboards/{id}`

One, as in the list. `404` if there is none, and also if the caller is not
offered it.

### `PUT /api/dashboards/{id}`

Replaces it. Admin-only. The body is the dashboard as `GET` answered it, with
`version` set to the version it was read at: **it is required**, and a save
that names a version that is no longer current is a `409` saying what the
current one is, because the alternative is quietly deleting what the last
person to save just built. The `id` may be left out of the body, `kind` cannot
change, and `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `updatedBy` are the server's and
ignored. `200` with the dashboard at the next version.

The wall board takes a `PUT` for its assignments (`roles`, `homeFor`,
`screens`, `position`) and nothing else: it has no cards, so one with cards is
a `400`. Its gauges are the board's tags, `GET` and `PUT
/api/board`.

### `DELETE /api/dashboards/{id}`

Admin-only. `{"deleted":"line-2"}`. Cards point at things and own nothing, so
nothing else is touched. The wall board is a `400`: it is always there.

Builds, saves and deletes are logged as `config` events on subject
`dashboard:<id>`.

## Webhooks

### `POST /api/webhook/{path}`

Fires every automation with a `webhook` trigger on that path. **No session and
no permission**: the path is the secret a third party is given, the same trust
model this endpoint has always had, and a SCADA system or a SaaS callback has
no account to log in with. Pick a path nobody could guess.

The body, up to 1 MiB, is handed to the rule. `202`
`{"accepted":"fill-now"}`. `404` `"no automation is listening on this webhook
path"` when nothing is: a webhook posting into nothing looks identical to one
that works, so it says so.

## Fleet

Registered edge relays, their live presence over Sparkplug, and commands to
them. Needs `HOTLOOP_FLEET_ENABLED`. See [FLEET.md](/gateway/fleet/).

### `GET /api/fleet`

```json
{"configured":true,"members":[{"id":"press-relay-01","name":"Press line relay","group":"plant-a","nodeId":"press-relay-01","statusUrl":"http://press-relay-01:8081","enabled":true,"createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:28:49.448323Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:28:49.448323Z","online":false,"polled":true,"error":"Get \"http://press-relay-01:8081/status\": dial tcp: lookup press-relay-01 on 10.89.0.1:53: no such host"}]}
```

`online` is from NBIRTH and NDEATH. `release` is the build the relay said it
runs in its last birth: `version`, `imageDigest` (when its supervisor says; the
Helm chart doesn't) and `since`, when the Gateway first heard that build. A
relay too old to report one has none. For a member with a `statusUrl`, `polled`
is true and `reachable`, `forwardQueueLen`, `devices`, `connected`, `config` and
`updateMode` (`auto` or `approve`) come from its `/status`; they mean nothing
when it was not reachable. With the feature off: `{"members":[],"configured":false}`.

### `POST /api/fleet`

Creates or replaces a member: `id`, `name`, `group` and `nodeId` (its Sparkplug
identity) required; `description`, `statusUrl` (`http://` or `https://`) and
`enabled` optional. Answers the member. This one works with the feature off,
so the fleet can be declared before it is switched on.

### `DELETE /api/fleet/{id}`

`{"deleted":"press-relay-01"}`, or `404`.

### `POST /api/fleet/{id}/rebirth`

Publishes a `Node Control/Rebirth` to the relay. No body.
`{"status":"rebirth requested"}`. `404` for an unknown member.

### `POST /api/fleet/{id}/restart`

Publishes `Node Control/Reboot`. `{"status":"restart requested"}`. Admin-only:
restarting a relay drops its data until it is back.

### `POST /api/fleet/{id}/update`

Approves the image update a relay is holding for. Publishes `Node Control/Update`.
`{"status":"update approved"}`. Admin-only: the relay exits and its supervisor
starts whatever image it follows, so it drops its data for the moment that takes.
It only does something to a relay set to `HOTLOOP_EDGE_RELAY_UPDATE_MODE=approve`;
any other relay logs that it ignored it. The request names no image: there is
nothing to put one in, which is the point. See
[EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/#updating-a-relay).

### `POST /api/fleet/{id}/config`

Pushes a new device file to the relay, which applies it live: no restart, its
broker session and forward queue kept, and every device the file didn't change
left connected. The body is **the device file itself**, raw JSON, not wrapped
in anything. It is validated before anything is published (`400` `"invalid
device file: ..."` if not). `{"status":"config pushed"}` means the broker took
it; whether the relay is running it is `config.digest` on that member in
`GET /api/fleet`, and a file the relay refused shows there as
`config.rejected`. Admin-only: it changes what the relay polls. See
[FLEET.md](/gateway/fleet/#config-push).

### `DELETE /api/fleet/{id}/config`

Takes the push back. Clears the retained config on the broker so no later boot
applies it, and a relay connected right now drops its pushed file and goes back
to its local device file live. No body. `{"status":"config push cleared"}`,
`404` for an unknown member, `503` when the Gateway isn't connected to the
broker. Admin-only, like pushing. It doesn't restart anything. Send it while
the relay is online: an offline relay never hears it. See
[EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/#where-a-pushed-file-lives-and-which-file-wins).

## Notifications

Paging a phone when an alarm is raised, over a webhook, SMTP, ntfy or Gotify, and
telling the next person when nobody acknowledges it. Needs
`HOTLOOP_NOTIFY_ENABLED`.

### `POST /api/notify/test`

Sends a synthetic alarm notification through every configured channel, now, so
you find out the SMTP relay rejects you before a real alarm does. No body. Needs
`HOTLOOP_NOTIFY_ENABLED`. Admin-only: it sends a real message and spends
whatever quota the provider allows.

```json
{"results":[{"channel":"smtp","success":true}]}
```

`200` whether or not each channel worked; each result says. A failed one
carries `error`. A failed webhook names its scheme and host and nothing else,
because for most paging services the URL is the credential. See
[NOTIFY.md](/iot/notifications/).

### `GET /api/notify/escalation`

The alarm escalation policy, the channels a step may name, and the chains open
right now. `available` is `false`, with an off policy and no channels, when
`HOTLOOP_NOTIFY_ENABLED` isn't set; the answer is still `200`. Admin-only for read
and write: the policy holds people's ntfy topics, which on a server anybody can
reach are passwords.

```json
{"available":true,"policy":{"enabled":true,"minPriority":"high","contacts":[{"name":"Ana","ntfyTopic":"ana-phone-3f9c","emails":["ana@plant.test"]}],"steps":[{"afterMinutes":5,"contacts":["Ana"]},{"afterMinutes":10,"channels":["gotify"]}],"repeatEveryMinutes":15,"repeatTimes":2},"channels":["smtp","ntfy","gotify"],"active":[{"alarmId":"boiler-hi","name":"Boiler Trip","raisedAt":"2026-10-21T03:00:00Z","sent":1,"total":4,"nextAt":"2026-10-21T03:15:00Z"}],"limits":{"steps":10,"contacts":50,"repeats":20,"minutes":1440}}
```

`channels` are the ones this HotLoop has configured, which is all a step can
name. `active` is every alarm being walked down the chain: how many sends have
gone out of how many the policy has (steps, then repeats), and when the next is
due. Nothing saved yet is `{"policy":{"enabled":false},...}`: off, with nothing in it.

### `PUT /api/notify/escalation`

Replaces the whole policy, not a patch, and answers what `GET` would. It applies
to alarms raised from now on. `400` when notifications aren't enabled.

```json
{"enabled":true,"minPriority":"high",
 "contacts":[{"name":"Ana","ntfyTopic":"ana-phone-3f9c","emails":["ana@plant.test"]}],
 "steps":[{"afterMinutes":5,"contacts":["Ana"]},{"afterMinutes":10,"channels":["gotify"]}],
 "repeatEveryMinutes":15,"repeatTimes":2}
```

`minPriority` is `critical`, `high` (the default), `medium` or `low`. A step is
due `afterMinutes` (1 to 1440) after the one before it, the first after the
raise, and names `contacts` from the list, `channels` the deployment has, or
both. At most 10 steps, 50 contacts and 20 repeats. Unknown fields are refused.

`400` with the reason when the policy can't work, in words you can act on: a
step that names nobody, a contact who isn't in the list, a channel this HotLoop
hasn't configured (the answer lists the ones it has), an ntfy topic with ntfy
not configured or an address with email not configured, an address that isn't a
plain one, a repeat with no interval. Nothing is stored when it is refused.
Saving it is in the system log, without the topics. See
[NOTIFY.md](/iot/notifications/#escalation).

### `POST /api/notify/ack/{token}`

The **Acknowledge** button on an ntfy notification. The phone pressing it has
no session to send, so there is **no session and no permission**: the signed
token in the path is the authorization, and all it authorizes is
acknowledging one occurrence of one alarm, once, before it expires
(`HOTLOOP_NOTIFY_ACK_TTL`, 12 hours by default). A button from yesterday's trip
cannot acknowledge today's. It is a `POST` on purpose: link previewers and
security scanners open links on their own, and an alarm must never be
acknowledged by a robot. No body. It answers with the alarm as acknowledged (the
shape, from the handler; the other examples in this document were captured from
a running Gateway, this one wasn't, because that Gateway had no ntfy):

```json
{"acknowledged":true,"alarmId":"extruder-temp-hi","name":"Extruder temperature high","state":"ack-active","ackedBy":"notify:ntfy"}
```

With acknowledge links switched off:

```json
{"error":"acknowledge links are not enabled on this HotLoop (they need HOTLOOP_PUBLIC_URL and a channel that carries a button)"}
```

It is an ordinary acknowledgement through the alarm engine, audited under
`notify:<channel>`. Every refusal is answered and logged, because a button that
silently did nothing looks exactly like one nobody pressed:

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 403 | Forged, altered, or signed with a different secret |
| 404 | The alarm no longer exists, or acknowledge links are off (they need `HOTLOOP_PUBLIC_URL` and a channel with a button) |
| 409 | Already used, the alarm was raised again since, or there is nothing left to acknowledge |
| 410 | Genuine, but expired |
| 503 | The acknowledgement could not be saved; the link is given back so a second press can still work |

The answer carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so the ntfy web app can
press it from its own origin; nothing on this route reads a cookie. The token
is never logged or returned anywhere. See
[NOTIFY.md](/iot/notifications/#acknowledge-links).

## Backups

Logical, table-data-only database snapshots. Needs `HOTLOOP_BACKUP_ENABLED`.
Both admin-only: a listing shows every table's row count, users and sessions
included. **There is no restore endpoint**, on purpose: restoring is a flag on
the binary, run once by somebody who knows the database is meant to receive it,
never a network call against a live one. See
[BACKUP.md](/iot/backup/#restoring-a-backup).

### `GET /api/backup`

The backups on the volume, each with its manifest.

```json
{"backups":[{"name":"20260927T202912Z","bytes":98567,"manifest":{"hotloopVersion":"4.16.0","schemaMigrations":["0001_core.sql","...","0007_service_audit.sql"],"createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:29:12.970721945Z","tables":[{"name":"devices","rows":2,"columns":[{"name":"id","type":"text"},{"name":"...","type":"..."}]}]}}],"configured":true}
```

### `POST /api/backup`

Takes one now and waits for it (up to 30 minutes: a big `tag_history` takes
a while). No body. Answers the manifest: version, migrations, and every
table's rows and columns.

## Scheduled reports

Historian summaries as CSV and HTML, on a schedule, by email or download.
Needs `HOTLOOP_REPORTS_ENABLED`. Viewers read, operators run, admins define:
a definition names where plant data gets emailed. See
[REPORTS.md](/gateway/reports/) for the definition's fields.

### `GET /api/reports`

```json
{"configured":true,"reports":[{"id":"line1-hourly","name":"Line 1 hourly","enabled":true,"tags":[{"deviceId":"extruder-1","tagName":"Temperature"},{"deviceId":"extruder-1","tagName":"Pressure"}],"window":{"count":1,"unit":"hours","end":"run_time"},"bucket":"window","aggregations":["min","max","avg"],"schedule":{"kind":"daily","at":"06:00"},"format":"both","recipients":["shift-lead@example.com"],"retain":10,"createdAt":"2026-09-27T20:29:23.300978Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-27T20:29:23.300978Z","nextRunAt":"2026-09-28T06:00:00Z"}],"smtpConfigured":true,"timezone":"UTC"}
```

Each definition carries `nextRunAt` and its most recent run as `lastRun`.

### `POST /api/reports`

Creates a definition; the body is the definition as above. `201`. `400` on a
failed validation (`"report line1-hourly: window end \"now\" must be run_time or
local_midnight"`), `409` if the id exists.

### `GET /api/reports/{id}`

One definition, as in the list. `404` for an unknown one.

### `PUT /api/reports/{id}`

Replaces the whole definition. The id cannot change (`400` if the body's
differs). `nextRunAt` and `lastRun` are accepted and ignored, so you can send
back what you read.

### `DELETE /api/reports/{id}`

Deletes it with its runs and files, cancelling a run in flight.
`{"deleted":"line1-hourly"}`, or `404`.

### `POST /api/reports/{id}/run`

Runs it now and waits. `?deliver=false` generates and stores it without
emailing anyone, for trying a definition out. `200` means the run happened;
its own `status` says whether the report worked. A run that fails is a result,
not a bad request, and it is recorded either way.

```json
{"id":1,"reportId":"line1-hourly","trigger":"manual","actor":"admin","status":"succeeded","startedAt":"2026-09-27T20:29:54.06926Z","finishedAt":"2026-09-27T20:29:54.092456655Z","windowStart":"2026-09-27T19:29:54.06926Z","windowEnd":"2026-09-27T20:29:54.06926Z","tags":2,"rows":2,"readings":984,"excluded":2,"files":[{"format":"csv","name":"20260927T202954Z-1.csv","bytes":338},{"format":"html","name":"20260927T202954Z-1.html","bytes":2430}],"emailStatus":"skipped","emailTo":["shift-lead@example.com"]}
```

`400` for a `deliver` that is not true or false, `404` for an unknown report.

### `GET /api/reports/{id}/runs`

`{"runs": [...]}`, newest first, `?limit=` default 50, at most 500. `404` for
an unknown report, not an empty list.

### `GET /api/reports/{id}/runs/{run}/download`

Streams one stored file as an attachment. `?format=csv` or `html`.

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="20260927T202954Z-1.csv"
Cache-Control: private, no-store

device_id,tag_name,unit,period_start,period_end,min,max,avg,excluded
extruder-1,Temperature,C,2026-09-27T19:29:54+00:00,2026-09-27T20:29:54+00:00,19.50001230192043,23.499980145373126,21.508905654397623,1
```

HTML is served with a `sandbox` Content-Security-Policy: a report is a document
to read, not a page that gets to run anything. The file opened is the one the
run record names; nothing in the URL becomes part of a path. `400` for a run
number that is not one or a format that is neither, `404` for a run or file
that does not exist.

## Sites

### `GET /api/sites`

Every site this Gateway federates, asked for its plant status over MCP in
parallel, 6 seconds each, so one dead site cannot hold up the rest. The sites
are the outbound MCP servers in the config. See
[MCP.md](/iot/mcp/#federating-sites).

```json
{"configured":true,
 "rollup":{"sites":2,"reachable":1,"devices":2,"connected":2,"tags":5,"outstandingAlarms":1,"unacknowledgedAlarms":1,"criticalAlarms":0},
 "sites":[{"name":"plant-a","reachable":true,"latencyMs":14,"plant":"Demo Plant","uptime":"1m25s","devices":2,"connected":2,"degraded":0,"disconnected":0,"tags":5,"outstandingAlarms":1,"unacknowledgedAlarms":1,"criticalAlarms":0,"writesEnabled":true},
          {"name":"plant-c","reachable":false,"error":"connect to MCP server \"plant-c\": calling \"initialize\": ... no such host","latencyMs":49,"devices":0,"connected":0,"degraded":0,"disconnected":0,"tags":0,"outstandingAlarms":0,"unacknowledgedAlarms":0,"criticalAlarms":0,"writesEnabled":false}]}
```

The counts of an unreachable site mean nothing and are left out of the
roll-up: counting a site you cannot reach as zero alarms would be the most
dangerous thing this screen could do. With no sites configured:
`{"configured":false,"sites":[]}`.

## Settings

### `GET /api/settings`

Every setting, its effective value, where the value came from and the variable
that sets it:

```json
{"groups":["Plant","Safety","Polling","Historian","Database","MCP","Server"],
 "settings":[{"key":"ui.plantName","group":"Plant","label":"Plant name","help":"...","value":"Demo Plant East","kind":"string","source":"stored","envVar":"HOTLOOP_PLANT_NAME","editable":true},
             {"key":"safety.allowWrites","group":"Safety","label":"Writes allowed","help":"...","value":true,"kind":"bool","source":"environment","envVar":"HOTLOOP_ALLOW_WRITES","editable":false},
             {"key":"database.password","group":"Database","label":"Password","help":"Never shown. It comes from the release Secret.","value":"set","kind":"secret","source":"environment","envVar":"HOTLOOP_DB_PASSWORD","editable":false}]}
```

`source` is `stored`, `environment` or `default`. A `secret` is only ever `set`
or `not set`. `envVar` is the variable the value came from. A few settings fall
back to a second variable when the `HOTLOOP_` one is blank (`TZ` for the
timezone, `POSTGRES_HOST`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER` and
`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` for the database), and when the fallback is what's in
effect, `envVar` names it. A variable set to an empty string counts as unset,
the same as the config treats it. The poll settings are shown in milliseconds,
but their variables take a duration (`5s`, `500ms`) or a bare number of seconds.

`product` in the `Server` group says which HotLoop this is. A feature this
product doesn't have that the deployment switched on anyway (say
`HOTLOOP_REPORTS_ENABLED=true` on IoT) doesn't stop it starting. It's logged
as a warning at startup and listed here in an extra group, `Not in this
product`, with its variable and a line saying where it lives. The setting is
left exactly as it is, so the same configuration on a product that has the
feature turns it on. With nothing like that set, the group isn't there.

### `PUT /api/settings`

Changes the plant-identity settings, and only those:

| Key | Type |
|---|---|
| `ui.plantName` | string, at most 200 characters |
| `ui.siteId` | string, at most 200 characters |
| `ui.timezone` | an IANA name this machine knows (`America/Chicago`) |
| `ui.confirmWrites` | bool |
| `ui.kioskIdleSeconds` | a whole number of seconds, 10 to 43200: how long a kiosk sign-in survives with nobody touching the panel. Default 900 |
| `ui.lockoutAttempts` | a whole number, 0 to 100: wrong passwords or PINs in a row that lock one account. Default 10, and 0 is no lockout |
| `ui.panelDelaySeconds` | a whole number of seconds, 0 to 30: the most a kiosk panel waits before checking the next PIN typed without a user name, after wrong ones. Default 3, and 0 is no wait |
| `ui.lockoutSeconds` | a whole number of seconds, 10 to 86400: how long a locked account stays locked. Default 300 |

```json
{"ui.plantName":"Demo Plant East","ui.timezone":"America/Chicago"}
```

Answers the full settings, as `GET` does. Any other key is a 400 naming it:

```json
{"error":"safety.allowWrites is set by the deployment and cannot be changed here"}
```

That is deliberate. The write switches decide whether this process can move
machinery, and a control that can be turned on from the same browser that
issues the writes is not a control. Changing them is a deployment.

## Historian targets

The plant's own databases, which HotLoop writes its history to as well as its
own. See [HISTORIAN-TARGETS.md](/iot/historian-targets/). Every role that reads the
settings sees them and how each one is doing. Changing one is admin only,
because a target is somewhere plant data goes. Passwords are sealed with the
device credential key (`HOTLOOP_SECRET_KEY_FILE`) and never answered with;
`passwordSet` says whether one is stored, and `passwordProblem` why a stored
one can't be opened. Every change goes on the log and takes effect at once.

### `GET /api/historian/targets`

```json
{"secretKey":true,
 "kinds":[{"id":"postgres","title":"PostgreSQL or TimescaleDB","defaultPort":5432,"defaultTable":"hotloop_history",
    "databaseLabel":"Database","tableLabel":"Table","passwordLabel":"Password","usesUsername":true,"usesOrg":false},
   {"id":"sqlserver","title":"Microsoft SQL Server","defaultPort":1433,"defaultTable":"hotloop_history",
    "databaseLabel":"Database","tableLabel":"Table","passwordLabel":"Password","usesUsername":true,"usesOrg":false},
   {"id":"mysql","title":"MySQL or MariaDB","defaultPort":3306,"defaultTable":"hotloop_history",
    "databaseLabel":"Database","tableLabel":"Table","passwordLabel":"Password","usesUsername":true,"usesOrg":false},
   {"id":"influxdb","title":"InfluxDB 2 or 3","defaultPort":8086,"defaultTable":"hotloop_history",
    "databaseLabel":"Bucket (InfluxDB 3: database)","tableLabel":"Measurement","passwordLabel":"API token",
    "usesUsername":false,"usesOrg":true}],
 "targets":[{"id":"plant-pg","name":"Plant historian","kind":"postgres","address":"db.plant.local:5432",
   "database":"plant","username":"hotloop","table":"hotloop_history","useTls":true,"insecureSkipVerify":false,
   "enabled":true,"createdBy":"admin","passwordSet":true,"createdAt":"2026-10-03T09:12:04Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-03T09:12:04Z",
   "status":{"state":"down","since":"2026-10-03T10:02:11Z","queued":50000,"queueCap":50000,"written":182340,
     "backfilled":0,"dropped":1210,"refused":0,"lastWrite":"2026-10-03T10:02:10Z",
     "lastError":"failed to connect to `user=hotloop database=plant`: dial tcp 10.20.0.9:5432: connect: connection refused",
     "owedFrom":"2026-10-03T10:02:09Z"}}]}
```

`kinds` are the databases this HotLoop writes to, and what each calls its
fields: InfluxDB has a token where the others have a password (`password`
carries it), a bucket where they have a database (`database`), a measurement
where they have a table (`table`), and an organization (`org`) none of them
have. `status.state` is `up`,
`catching-up` (up, and still sending what it's owed from HotLoop's own
history), `down`, `starting` or `off` (switched off). `queued` is what's
waiting in memory, out of `queueCap`. `written` counts readings sent live and
`backfilled` the ones sent from HotLoop's own history. `dropped` counts
readings the queue let go while the target couldn't keep up: they're owed,
not lost. `refused` counts readings the database itself wouldn't take, with
its reason in `lastRefusal`. `owedFrom` and `owedTo` are what's still owed;
`owedTo` is missing while the end is still open, which it is for as long as
the target is down.

### `POST /api/historian/targets`

```json
{"id":"plant-pg","name":"Plant historian","kind":"postgres","address":"db.plant.local","database":"plant",
 "username":"hotloop","password":"...","useTls":true}
```

`id` is 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and `-`, and names the target in the
system log. `address` is `host` or `host:port`, with no login in it; the
kind's default port fills in a missing one. `table` defaults to the kind's
`defaultTable` and may carry a schema (`history.hotloop`). `org` is
InfluxDB 2's organization. `enabled` defaults to true. A password needs a key:
without `HOTLOOP_SECRET_KEY_FILE` it's a `400`, never stored in the clear.
`201` with the target and its status; `409` for an id that's taken.

### `PUT /api/historian/targets/{id}`

Any of the fields above but `id`; what isn't sent stays. `"password":""`
clears the password. A change starts the target over with its new settings,
and what it was owed is still owed. `200` with the target.

### `DELETE /api/historian/targets/{id}`

Stops writing to it and forgets what it was owed. What it already holds stays
in its database. Switch it off with `"enabled":false` instead to keep the
settings. `200` `{"deleted":"plant-pg"}`.

## System log

### `GET /api/events`

Every change, write, login and connection transition, newest first.

| Query | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| `category` | Repeatable: `system`, `device`, `tag`, `write`, `alarm`, `automation`, `mcp`, `config`, `auth` |
| `severity` | Repeatable: `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error` |
| `subject` | Exactly: a device id, a tag key, an entity_id, `equipment:4`, `label:critical` |
| `q` | Case-insensitive search |
| `minutes` | Only the last N minutes |
| `limit` | Default 200, at most 5000 |

```json
[{"id":61,"at":"2026-09-27T20:29:23.303795Z","severity":"info","category":"config","subject":"line1-hourly","actor":"admin","message":"report created"}]
```

`actor` is a user, `system`, `automation:<id>` or `mcp:<client>`. `detail`,
when there is one, is extra JSON as a string.

## Logbook

### `GET /api/logbook`

One timeline of what happened, newest first: entity state changes, writes,
alarm transitions, automation and script runs, and configuration changes and
service calls from the system log. The trails are read where they are and merged, so
each keeps its own retention. Numeric readings are not in it: that is what
`GET /api/history` is for. See [LOGBOOK.md](/iot/logbook/).

| Query | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| `entity` | Only what is about this entity: its state changes, writes to it and its tags, its alarms, the automation runs it triggers or that wrote to it, config changes to it |
| `equipment_id` | Only what happened at this node of the equipment tree or under it, by the same rule. Not with `entity` |
| `actor` | Case-insensitive part of who did it: a user, `automation:<id>`, `mcp:<client>` |
| `kinds` | Comma-separated or repeated: `state`, `write`, `alarm`, `automation`, `event`, `script`, `recipe` |
| `from`, `to` | RFC 3339 times; `from` inclusive, `to` exclusive |
| `limit` | Default 100, at most 1000 |
| `before` | The `next` of the previous page |

```json
{"entries":[
  {"at":"2026-09-28T09:14:02.51Z","kind":"state","id":41,"severity":"info","message":"changed to on (was off)","entity_id":"switch.tank_farm_pump","old_state":"off","state":"on","quality":"good"},
  {"at":"2026-09-28T09:14:02.18Z","kind":"write","id":88,"severity":"info","message":"wrote true to tank-farm/pump (switch.turn_on on switch.tank_farm_pump) (was 0)","actor":"admin","source":"ui","entity_id":"switch.tank_farm_pump","device_id":"tank-farm","tag":"tank-farm/pump","call_id":"5c9f8545a93b5443"},
  {"at":"2026-09-28T09:13:40.02Z","kind":"state","id":37,"severity":"info","message":"changed to closed (was open); 14 changes before this not logged, it was changing faster than the logbook records","entity_id":"valve.infeed","old_state":"open","state":"closed","quality":"good","suppressed":14}
 ],
 "next":"MjAyNi0wOS0yOFQwOToxMzo0MC4wMlp8c3RhdGV8Mzc"}
```

`id` is the row's id in its own trail (for a state change, the entity's
immutable id), and with `at` and `kind` it is what `next` encodes: the page
after this one is everything strictly older in that order, whatever was
added in the meantime. `next` is left out on the last page. `suppressed` is
how many changes of that entity before this one were not logged, because it
was changing faster than ten at once and then one every two seconds.

`400` for an unknown kind, a malformed time, `from` not before `to`, a
limit over 1000, a made-up cursor, or `entity` and `equipment_id` together;
`404` for a node that does not exist. `503` when the logbook is not running
in the process answering.

## Live feed

### `GET /api/stream`

Server-sent events, one way, for as long as you hold it open. SSE rather than
a WebSocket because the traffic only goes one way, and an event stream
reconnects on its own when the pod restarts under an open dashboard.
`EventSource` sends the session cookie; a script sends the bearer token.

On connect you get `retry: 3000` and then the current picture, so a screen is
populated before anything changes:

```
retry: 3000

event: snapshot
data: [{"deviceId":"extruder-1","protocol":"opcua","tagName":"Temperature","tagValue":19.553128777917983,"unit":"C","quality":"good","timestamp":"2026-09-27T20:34:23.619589Z"}]

event: alarms
data: {"alarms":[...outstanding alarms...],"summary":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0,"unacked":0,"total":1}}

event: entities
data: {"changed":[...every entity state...],"removed":[]}
```

Then, as things happen:

| Event | Data | When |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | An array of readings, the `GET /api/values` shape, newest per tag | Every 250 ms, if anything changed. Coalesced: a plant making five thousand readings a second must not push five thousand messages a second at a browser that repaints sixty times |
| `entities` | `{"changed": [states], "removed": [entity_ids]}` | Every 250 ms, if any entity state changed. `removed` is an entity disabled, deleted or renamed away from |
| `alarm` | `{"alarm": {...}, "event": "shelved"}`, the alarm and what happened to it (`raised`, `acked`, `cleared`, `shelved`, `unshelved`, `suppressed`, `unsuppressed`) | Immediately: alarm transitions are rare and each one matters |
| `device` | `{"deviceId":"tank-farm","state":"connected"}` | Immediately: the screen should go red when a device drops, not at the next flush |
| `logbook` | `{"kinds":["state","write"]}`, which kinds of logbook entry have something new | At most once a second. No entries in it, because what a screen should show depends on its filters: it asks `GET /api/logbook` for its own page |

```
event: alarm
data: {"alarm":{"definitionId":"extruder-temp-hi","state":"shelved","shelvedUntil":"2026-09-27T20:39:45.839983854Z","shelvedBy":"admin","...":"..."},"event":"shelved"}

event: device
data: {"deviceId":"tank-farm","state":"connected"}
```

A comment line (`: heartbeat 2026-09-27T20:35:00Z`) every 20 seconds keeps
proxies from closing an idle connection. A client that cannot keep up misses
`values` and `entities` updates rather than stalling everyone else; the next
one carries current values, so nothing is lost for long. The response sets
`X-Accel-Buffering: no`, because a buffering proxy turns a live feed into a
very slow download.

The stream looks at its session again every five seconds and closes when the
session is gone: signed out, expired, revoked, or the account disabled or no
longer allowed `status.read`. It sends no event first. A browser's
`EventSource` reconnects, gets the `401` above, and stops. With
`HOTLOOP_AUTH_INSECURE=true` there is no session and nothing to check. The
check does not count as the session being used, so a screen left open does not
keep a session fresh.

## MCP

### `/mcp` and `/mcp/`

The Model Context Protocol, streamable HTTP transport, for agents. Any method:
the transport uses `POST` for calls, `GET` for the server's own stream and
`DELETE` to end a session. The path is `HOTLOOP_MCP_PATH` (`/mcp` by default)
and the endpoint is only there when `HOTLOOP_MCP_ENABLED` is on.

It is **not** behind the session login. It has its own bearer token,
`HOTLOOP_MCP_TOKEN`, checked in front of the handler so that a caller without it
cannot even list the tools:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="hotloop"

unauthorized
```

With no token configured the endpoint is open, which is only reasonable behind
a NetworkPolicy, and startup says so in the log. An agent is a caller like any
other: its writes go through the same write gate, narrowed further by
`HOTLOOP_ALLOW_MCP_WRITES`, and are audited as `mcp:<client name>`. The tools
and resources are in [MCP.md](/iot/mcp/).

```
POST /mcp
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"1"}}}
```

answers with an `Mcp-Session-Id` header and the server's capabilities and
instructions.

## The UI

### `GET /static/`

The stylesheet, scripts and icon, straight out of the binary, cacheable but
revalidated so a redeployed pod never serves a stale script to a page that is
still open. The page itself does not need them (it carries its own inline);
they are here for anything that wants them separately. No session: they are
the same for everyone.

### `GET /manifest.webmanifest`

The web app manifest that lets a phone install the UI as an app: the product and
plant name, `display` `standalone`, the theme colors, the icons (192 and 512
pixel PNGs, a maskable 512 and the SVG) and shortcuts to Alarms and Dashboards.
Every URL in it is relative to the manifest's own, so it is right wherever HotLoop
is mounted. The name follows the plant name set in Settings, and the answer is
`Cache-Control: no-cache` so a rename shows on the next look. No session: a phone
asks before anybody has signed in. See
[DASHBOARDS.md](/iot/dashboards/#on-a-phone).

### `GET /sw.js`

The service worker, at the root of where HotLoop is mounted so its scope covers
the whole app. It keeps the page and the last answer to the reads a person looks
at, and answers them marked as old when HotLoop can't be reached. It never answers,
keeps or queues a write. The running version is in it, so each release gets a page
cache of its own. `Cache-Control: no-cache`; no session. Only a browser in a secure
context (https, or `localhost`) runs it.

### `/`

The single page, with its stylesheet and scripts inline so it renders the same
at the root of a host, under a path, or inside the EmberNet dashboard's iframe.
Gzipped when the browser asks. `GET` and `HEAD` only; any other method is `405`.
Any other path that no route matches lands here and gets a `404`, because
serving the page for a typo would make it look like a working screen. No
session: the page is the login form until you log in.
